text: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Washa, from Hammad Bin Usman, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws, said, ‘I heard himasws saying: ‘Rasool-Allahsaww Fasted until it was said, ‘Hesaww would not break’. Then hesaww broke (did not Fast) until it was said, ‘Hesaww will never Fast’. Then hesaww Fasted the Fasts of Dawoodas, one day, and one day not. Then hesaww passed away upon Fasting three days during the month. These (three Fasts) equate to Fasting the (whole) month, and they remove Al-Wahr of the chest, and Al-Wahr is the anxiety’. Hammad (the narrator) said, ‘So I said, ‘And which days are these?’ Heasws said: ‘The first Thursday in the month, and the first Wednesday after the ten (days) from it, and the last Thursday in it’. So I said, ‘How did these days come to be the one in which is to be Fasting’. So heasws said: ‘The ones before us from the communities, whenever the Punishment descended upon any one of these, descended during these days. Thus, Rasool-Allahsaww Fasted during these days, out of fear (upon the Punishment on hissaww community’).

citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُهُ يَقُولُ صَامَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) حَتَّى قِيلَ مَا يُفْطِرُ ثُمَّ أَفْطَرَ حَتَّى قِيلَ مَا يَصُومُ ثُمَّ صَامَ صَوْمَ دَاوُدَ ( عليه السلام ) يَوْماً وَ يَوْماً لَا ثُمَّ قُبِضَ عَلَى صِيَامِ ثَلَاثَةِ أَيَّامٍ فِي الشَّهْرِ قَالَ إِنَّهُنَّ يَعْدِلْنَ صَوْمَ الشَّهْرِ وَ يَذْهَبْنَ بِوَحَرِ الصَّدْرِ وَ الْوَحَرُ الْوَسْوَسَةُ قَالَ حَمَّادٌ فَقُلْتُ وَ أَيُّ الْأَيَّامِ هِيَ قَالَ أَوَّلُ خَمِيسٍ فِي الشَّهْرِ وَ أَوَّلُ أَرْبِعَاءَ بَعْدَ الْعَشْرِ مِنْهُ وَ آخِرُ خَمِيسٍ فِيهِ فَقُلْتُ كَيْفَ صَارَتْ هَذِهِ الْأَيَّامُ الَّتِي تُصَامُ فَقَالَ إِنَّ مَنْ قَبْلَنَا مِنَ الْأُمَمِ كَانَ إِذَا نَزَلَ عَلَى أَحَدِهِمُ الْعَذَابُ نَزَلَ فِي هَذِهِ الْأَيَّامِ فَصَامَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) هَذِهِ الْأَيَّامَ الْمَخُوفَةَ .

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abu Ayoub, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, at the beginning of his<sup>saww</sup> Sending, was Fasting such until it was said, ‘He<sup>saww</sup> will not be breaking (stop Fasting)’, and he<sup>saww</sup> was breaking (not Fasting) until it was said, ‘He<sup>saww</sup> will not be Fasting’. Then he<sup>saww</sup> left that and Fasted for one day, and broke (not Fasted) for one day, and it is the Fasting of Dawood<sup>as</sup>. Then he<sup>saww</sup> left that and Fasted the three days of brightness (13<sup>th</sup>, 14<sup>th</sup> & 15<sup>th</sup> of the month). Then he<sup>saww</sup> left that and separated these during every ten days, there being two Thursdays and one Wednesday in between. So he<sup>saww</sup> passed away, and he<sup>saww</sup> was acting upon that’.

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Jameel Bin Slih, from Muhammad Bin Marwan who said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> was Fasting such, until it was said, ‘He<sup>saww</sup> would not be breaking (not Fasting)’. Then he<sup>saww</sup> Fasted one day, and broke one day. Then he<sup>saww</sup> Fasted Mondays and Thursdays. Then he<sup>saww</sup> transferred from that to the Fasting of three days during the month, the first Thursday at the beginning of the month, and Wednesday in the middle of the month, and Thursday at the end of the month; and he<sup>saww</sup> was saying: ‘That is the Fasting of the whole time (whole month)’. And my<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> was saying: ‘There is no one more hateful to me<sup>asws</sup> than a man to whom it is said, ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> used to do such and such’, so he is saying, ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> will not Punish me if I strive hard regarding the Prayer’. It is as if he sees that Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> neglected something from the preferential acts being frustrated from it’.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hafs Bin Al Bakhtary, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The wives of the Prophet<sup>saww</sup>, whenever they had compensatory Fasts upon them, would delay that to Shaban in anticipation that Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> would forbid them. So whenever it was Shaban, they would Fast these, and Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> was saying: ‘Shaban is my<sup>saww</sup> month’.

citation.arabic_text: كُنَّ نِسَاءُ النَّبِيِّ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) إِذَا كَانَ عَلَيْهِنَّ صِيَامٌ أَخَّرْنَ ذَلِكَ إِلَى شَعْبَانَ كَرَاهَةَ أَنْ يَمْنَعْنَ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) فَإِذَا كَانَ شَعْبَانُ صُمْنَ وَ كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) يَقُولُ شَعْبَانُ شَهْرِي .

text: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, altogether from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Al Halby who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘Did anyone from yourasws forefathersasws Fast during Shaban at all?’ Heasws said: ‘The best of myasws forefathersasws, Rasool-Allahsaww Fasted it’. Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa Bin Ubeyd, from Yunus, from Ibn Muskan, from Al Halby, from Abu Abdullahasws – similar to it. So, as for what has come regarding the Fasts of Shaban, heasws was asked about it, so heasws said: ‘Rasool-Allahsaww did not Fast it, nor did anyone from myasws forefathersasws’. Heasws said: ‘That is because a group was saying that Fasting in it is Obligatory like the Fasts of the Month of Ramazan, and its Obligation is like the Obligation of the Month of Ramazan, and that the one who breaks a day from it, so upon him would be the expiation similar to what it would be upon the one who breaks one day from the Month of Ramazan’. And rather, the words of the Scholarasws: ‘Rasool-Allahsaww did not Fast it, nor did anyone from myasws forefathersasws’, yes, hesaww did not Fast it as an Obligated Obligation, in belying the words of the one who alleged that it is an Obligation. And rather, Fasting it is a Sunnah wherein is virtue, and there is not upon the one who does not Fast it, anything’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) هَلْ صَامَ أَحَدٌ مِنْ آبَائِكَ شَعْبَانَ قَطُّ قَالَ صَامَهُ خَيْرُ آبَائِي رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) . عَلِيُّ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى بْنِ عُبَيْدٍ عَنْ يُونُسَ عَنِ ابْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنِ الْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) مِثْلَهُ فَأَمَّا الَّذِي جَاءَ فِي صَوْمِ شَعْبَانَ أَنَّهُ سُئِلَ ( عليه السلام ) عَنْهُ فَقَالَ مَا صَامَهُ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) وَ لَا أَحَدٌ مِنْ آبَائِي قَالَ ذَلِكَ لِأَنَّ قَوْماً قَالُوا إِنَّ صِيَامَهُ فَرْضٌ مِثْلُ صِيَامِ شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ وَ وُجُوبَهُ مِثْلُ وُجُوبِ شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ وَ إِنَّ مَنْ أَفْطَرَ يَوْماً مِنْهُ فَعَلَيْهِ مِنَ الْكَفَّارَةِ مِثْلُ مَا عَلَى مَنْ أَفْطَرَ يَوْماً مِنْ شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ وَ إِنَّمَا قَوْلُ الْعَالِمِ ( عليه السلام ) مَا صَامَهُ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) وَ لَا أَحَدٌ مِنْ آبَائِي ( عليهم السلام ) أَيْ مَا صَامُوهُ فَرْضاً وَاجِباً تَكْذِيباً لِقَوْلِ مَنْ زَعَمَ أَنَّهُ فَرْضٌ وَ إِنَّمَا كَانُوا يَصُومُونَهُ سُنَّةً فِيهَا فَضْلٌ وَ لَيْسَ عَلَى مَنْ لَمْ يَصُمْهُ شَيْ‏ءٌ
citation.translation: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, altogether from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Al Halby who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘Did anyone from yourasws forefathersasws Fast during Shaban at all?’ Heasws said: ‘The best of myasws forefathersasws, Rasool-Allahsaww Fasted it’. Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa Bin Ubeyd, from Yunus, from Ibn Muskan, from Al Halby, from Abu Abdullahasws – similar to it. So, as for what has come regarding the Fasts of Shaban, heasws was asked about it, so heasws said: ‘Rasool-Allahsaww did not Fast it, nor did anyone from myasws forefathersasws’. Heasws said: ‘That is because a group was saying that Fasting in it is Obligatory like the Fasts of the Month of Ramazan, and its Obligation is like the Obligation of the Month of Ramazan, and that the one who breaks a day from it, so upon him would be the expiation similar to what it would be upon the one who breaks one day from the Month of Ramazan’. And rather, the words of the Scholarasws: ‘Rasool-Allahsaww did not Fast it, nor did anyone from myasws forefathersasws’, yes, hesaww did not Fast it as an Obligated Obligation, in belying the words of the one who alleged that it is an Obligation. And rather, Fasting it is a Sunnah wherein is virtue, and there is not upon the one who does not Fast it, anything’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (16/254)

text: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hassan, from Ahmad in Sabeeh, from Anbasa Al Aabid who said, ‘The Prophet<sup>saww</sup> passed away upon Fasting Shaban and Ramazaan, and three days during every month – the first Thursday, and the middle Wednesday, and the last Thursday; and Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> and Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, both were Fasting that’.

citation.arabic_text: قُبِضَ النَّبِيُّ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) عَلَى صَوْمِ شَعْبَانَ وَ رَمَضَانَ وَ ثَلَاثَةِ أَيَّامٍ فِي كُلِّ شَهْرٍ أَوَّلِ خَمِيسٍ وَ أَوْسَطِ أَرْبِعَاءَ وَ آخِرِ خَمِيسٍ وَ كَانَ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ وَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) يَصُومَانِ ذَلِكَ .
citation.translation: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hassan, from Ahmad in Sabeeh, from Anbasa Al Aabid who said, ‘The Prophet<sup>saww</sup> passed away upon Fasting Shaban and Ramazaan, and three days during every month – the first Thursday, and the middle Wednesday, and the last Thursday; and Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> and Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, both were Fasting that’.

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, and Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Salma Sahib Al Sabiry, from Abu Al Sabbah Al Kinany who said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Fasting Shaban and Month of Ramazaan consecutively, is a (self) punishment from Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>!’

citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ صَوْمُ شَعْبَانَ وَ شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ مُتَتَابِعَيْنِ تَوْبَةٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَ اللَّهِ

text: A number of our companins, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Ali Bin Al Salt, from Zur’at Bin Muhammad, from Sama’at and from Mufazzal Bin Umar, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Ali<sup>asws</sup> used to link what is between Shaban and Ramazan, and he<sup>asws</sup> was saying: ‘Fasting two months consecutively is a (self) punishment from Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’.

citation.arabic_text: كَانَ عَلِيُّ بْنُ الْحُسَيْنِ ( عليه السلام ) يَصِلُ مَا بَيْنَ شَعْبَانَ وَ رَمَضَانَ وَ يَقُولُ صَوْمُ شَهْرَيْنِ مُتَتَابِعَيْنِ تَوْبَةٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ .

text: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Husayn Bin Ulwan, from Amro Bin Khalid, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> used to Fast Shaban and Ramazan and was linking the two, and he<sup>saww</sup> forbade the people that they link these two, and he<sup>saww</sup> was saying; ‘These two are the months of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and they are both an expiation from the sins for what was before them and for what is after them’.

citation.arabic_text: كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) يَصُومُ شَعْبَانَ وَ رَمَضَانَ يَصِلُهُمَا وَ يَنْهَى النَّاسَ أَنْ يَصِلُوهُمَا وَ كَانَ يَقُولُ هُمَا شَهْرَا اللَّهِ وَ هُمَا كَفَّارَةٌ لِمَا قَبْلَهُمَا وَ لِمَا بَعْدَهُمَا مِنَ الذُّنُوبِ .

text: Ali Bin Muhammad, from one of his companions, from Muhammad Bin Suleyman, from his father who said, ‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘What are youasws saying regarding the man who is Fasting Shaban and Month of Ramazan?’ So heasws said: ‘Both are month for which Allahazwj Blessed and High Said [4:92] two months successively: a penance from Allah’. I said, ‘So he should not keep a gap between the two?’ Heasws said: ‘When he breaks at night, so it is a gap, and rather, Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘Do not link regarding the Fasts’, meaning, the man should not Fast for two days continuously without breaking, and it is recommended for the servant that he should not leave the pre-dawn meal’.

citation.arabic_text: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) مَا تَقُولُ فِي الرَّجُلِ يَصُومُ شَعْبَانَ وَ شَهْرَ رَمَضَانَ فَقَالَ هُمَا الشَّهْرَانِ اللَّذَانِ قَالَ اللَّهُ تَبَارَكَ وَ تَعَالَى شَهْرَيْنِ مُتَتابِعَيْنِ تَوْبَةً مِنَ اللَّهِ قُلْتُ فَلَا يَفْصِلُ بَيْنَهُمَا قَالَ إِذَا أَفْطَرَ مِنَ اللَّيْلِ فَهُوَ فَصْلٌ وَ إِنَّمَا قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) لَا وِصَالَ فِي صِيَامٍ يَعْنِي لَا يَصُومُ الرَّجُلُ يَوْمَيْنِ مُتَوَالِيَيْنِ مِنْ غَيْرِ إِفْطَارٍ وَ قَدْ يُسْتَحَبُّ لِلْعَبْدِ أَنْ لَا يَدَعَ السَّحُورَ .

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having been asked about the Fast during the presence at home, so heasws said: ‘Three days during every month – the Thursday from a week, and the Wednesday from a week, and the Thursday from another week’. And heasws said: ‘Amir Al-Momineenasws said: ‘Fasting a month is the patience, and three days from every month removes temptation from the chests, and Fasting three days from every month is Fasting for the whole time. Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic is Saying [6:160] Whoever comes with a good deed, he shall have ten like it’.

citation.arabic_text: الْحَضَرِ فَقَالَ ثَلَاثَةُ أَيَّامٍ فِي كُلِّ شَهْرٍ الْخَمِيسُ مِنْ جُمْعَةٍ وَ الْأَرْبِعَاءُ مِنْ جُمْعَةٍ وَ الْخَمِيسُ مِنْ جُمْعَةٍ أُخْرَى وَ قَالَ قَالَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) صِيَامُ شَهْرِ الصَّبْرِ وَ ثَلَاثَةِ أَيَّامٍ مِنْ كُلِّ شَهْرٍ يَذْهَبْنَ بِبَلَابِلِ الصُّدُورِ وَ صِيَامُ ثَلَاثَةِ أَيَّامٍ مِنْ كُلِّ شَهْرٍ صِيَامُ الدَّهْرِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ يَقُولُ مَنْ جاءَ بِالْحَسَنَةِ فَلَهُ عَشْرُ أَمْثالِها .

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr who said, ‘I asked Abu Al-Hassanasws about the Fasts during the month, how are these (to be done)?’ Heasws said: ‘Three during the month, in every ten days. Allahazwj Blessed and High is Saying [6:160] Whoever comes with a good deed, he shall have ten like it – three days during the month is Fasting for the whole time’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا الْحَسَنِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنِ الصِّيَامِ فِي الشَّهْرِ كَيْفَ هُوَ قَالَ ثَلَاثٌ فِي الشَّهْرِ فِي كُلِّ عَشْرٍ يَوْمٌ إِنَّ اللَّهَ تَبَارَكَ وَ تَعَالَى يَقُولُ مَنْ جاءَ بِالْحَسَنَةِ فَلَهُ عَشْرُ أَمْثالِها ثَلَاثَةُ أَيَّامٍ فِي الشَّهْرِ صَوْمُ الدَّهْرِ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr who said, ‘I asked Abu Al-Hassanasws about the Fasts during the month, how are these (to be done)?’ Heasws said: ‘Three during the month, in every ten days. Allahazwj Blessed and High is Saying [6:160] Whoever comes with a good deed, he shall have ten like it – three days during the month is Fasting for the whole time’.

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Al Husayn Bin Mukharaq Abu Junada Al Salouly, from Abu Hamza, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’farasws, from hisasws fatherasws having said: ‘Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘The one who Fasts Shaban, for him would be purification from every slip, and Wasima and Badira’. Abu Hamza said, ‘I sid to Abu Ja’farasws, ‘What is Al-Wasima?’ Heasws said: ‘The oath regarding the disobedience and the vow regarding the disobedience’. I said, ‘So what is the Badira?’ Heasws said: ‘The oath during the anger, and the repenting from it, the regret’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) مَنْ صَامَ شَعْبَانَ كَانَ لَهُ طُهْراً مِنْ كُلِّ زَلَّةٍ وَ وَصْمَةٍ وَ بَادِرَةٍ قَالَ أَبُو حَمْزَةَ قُلْتُ لِأَبِي جَعْفَرٍ ( عليه السلام ) مَا الْوَصْمَةُ قَالَ الْيَمِينُ فِي الْمَعْصِيَةِ وَ النَّذْرُ فِي الْمَعْصِيَةِ قُلْتُ فَمَا الْبَادِرَةُ قَالَ الْيَمِينُ عِنْدَ الْغَضَبِ وَ التَّوْبَةُ مِنْهَا النَّدَمُ .

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Zurara who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the most meritorious of what the Sunnah flowed with regarding the voluntary from the Fasts’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Three days during the month – the Thursday in the beginning of the month, and the Wednesday in the middle of the month, and the Thursday in the end of the month’. I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘This is the entirety of what the Sunnah has flowed with regarding the Fast?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes’.

I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘This is the entirety of what the Sunnah has flowed with regarding the Fast?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes’.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, form Hammad, from Hareyz who said, ‘It was said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘What has come regarding the Fasting during the Wednesday?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Created the Fire on the day of Wednesday, thus its Fasting is Obligated in order to seek Refuge by it, from the Fire’.

citation.arabic_text: قِيلَ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) مَا جَاءَ فِي الصَّوْمِ فِي يَوْمِ الْأَرْبِعَاءِ فَقَالَ قَالَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ خَلَقَ النَّارَ يَوْمَ الْأَرْبِعَاءِ فَأَوْجَبَ صَوْمَهُ لِيُتَعَوَّذَ بِهِ مِنَ النَّارِ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, form Hammad, from Hareyz who said, ‘It was said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘What has come regarding the Fasting during the Wednesday?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Created the Fire on the day of Wednesday, thus its Fasting is Obligated in order to seek Refuge by it, from the Fire’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (6/258)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al hakam, from Hisham Bin Salim, from Al Ahowl, from Ibn Sinan, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> that Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> was asked about the Fasting of the two Thursdays, between the two being a Wednesday, so he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘As for the Thursday, so it is a day wherein the deeds are presented, and as for the Wednesday, so it is a day in which the Fire was Created, and as for the Fast, so it is a shield from the Fire’.

citation.arabic_text: أَمَّا الْخَمِيسُ فَيَوْمٌ تُعْرَضُ فِيهِ الْأَعْمَالُ وَ أَمَّا الْأَرْبِعَاءُ فَيَوْمٌ خُلِقَتْ فِيهِ النَّارُ وَ أَمَّا الصَّوْمُ فَجُنَّةٌ مِنَ النَّارِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al hakam, from Hisham Bin Salim, from Al Ahowl, from Ibn Sinan, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> that Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> was asked about the Fasting of the two Thursdays, between the two being a Wednesday, so he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘As for the Thursday, so it is a day wherein the deeds are presented, and as for the Wednesday, so it is a day in which the Fire was Created, and as for the Fast, so it is a shield from the Fire’.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa Bin Ubeyd, from Yunus, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘But rather, one should Fast the day of Wednesday, because no past community has been Punished except during the day of Wednesday in the middle of the month. Thus, it is recommended that one Fasts that day’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ إِنَّمَا يُصَامُ يَوْمُ الْأَرْبِعَاءِ لِأَنَّهُ لَمْ تُعَذَّبْ أُمَّةٌ فِيمَا مَضَى إِلَّا فِي يَوْمِ الْأَرْبِعَاءِ وَسَطِ الشَّهْرِ فَيُسْتَحَبُّ أَنْ يُصَامَ ذَلِكَ الْيَوْمُ .

text: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Imran, from Ziyad Al Qandy, from Abdullah Bin Sinan who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Whenever there are two Thursdays during the beginning of the month, so Fast the first of the two, for it is preferable; and whenever there was two Thursdays during the end of the month, so Fast the last of the two, for it is preferable’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ لِي أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) إِذَا كَانَ فِي أَوَّلِ الشَّهْرِ خَمِيسَانِ فَصُمْ أَوَّلَهُمَا فَإِنَّهُ أَفْضَلُ وَ إِذَا كَانَ فِي آخِرِ الشَّهْرِ خَمِيسَانِ فَصُمْ آخِرَهُمَا فَإِنَّهُ أَفْضَلُ .

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Shuayb, from Abu Baseer, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the pre-dawn meal for the one who intends to Fast, is it Obligatory upon him?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem if he does not partake the pre-dawn meal if he so desires to; and as for during the Month of Ramazan, so it is preferable that he partakes the pre-dawn meal. We<sup>asws</sup> love it that he does not neglect it during the Month of Ramazan’.

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from his brother Al Hassan, from Zur’at, from Sama’at who said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the pre-dawn meal for the one who intends to Fasting, so he<sup>asws</sup> said; ‘As for during the Month of Ramazan, so it is preferred with regards to the pre-dawn meal, and even though it may be by drinking from the water; and as for during the voluntary Fasts, so the one who loves that he partakes the pre-dawn meal, so let him do so, and the one who does not do it, so there is no problem’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ السَّحُورِ لِمَنْ أَرَادَ الصَّوْمَ فَقَالَ أَمَّا فِي شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ فَإِنَّ الْفَضْلَ فِي السَّحُورِ وَ لَوْ بِشَرْبَةٍ مِنْ مَاءٍ وَ أَمَّا فِي التَّطَوُّعِ فَمَنْ أَحَبَّ أَنْ يَتَسَحَّرَ فَلْيَفْعَلْ وَ مَنْ لَمْ يَفْعَلْ فَلَا بَأْسَ .

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, from his<sup>asws</sup> forefathers<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The pre-dawn meal is a Blessing’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘My<sup>saww</sup> community should not leave the pre-dawn meal, and even if it was upon stems (remaining after harvest)’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) السَّحُورُ بَرَكَةٌ قَالَ وَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) لَا تَدَعُ أُمَّتِيَ السَّحُورَ وَ لَوْ عَلَى حَشَفَةٍ .

For You<sup>azwj</sup>, we Fast, and upon Your<sup>azwj</sup> sustenance we break, therefore Accept it from us. The thirst is gone, and the veins are wet, and the Recompense remains (outstanding)’.

citation.arabic_text: اللَّهُمَّ لَكَ صُمْنَا وَ عَلَى رِزْقِكَ أَفْطَرْنَا فَتَقَبَّلْهُ مِنَّا ذَهَبَ الظَّمَأُ وَ ابْتَلَّتِ الْعُرُوقُ وَ بَقِيَ الْأَجْرُ

text: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Ahmad Bin Is’haq, from Sa’dan, from Abu Baseer, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘One should be saying during every night from the Month of Ramazan, during the breaking of the Fast up to its end, ‘The Praise is for Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, Who Aided us, so we Fasted, and Graced us, so we broke. O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Accept from us, and Aid us upon it, and Secure us in it, and Receive is from us in ease from You<sup>azwj</sup> and good health. The Praise is for Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, Who Accomplished for us one day from the Month of Ramazan’.

citation.arabic_text: تَقُولُ فِي كُلِّ لَيْلَةٍ مِنْ شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ عِنْدَ الْإِفْطَارِ إِلَى آخِرِهِ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي أَعَانَنَا فَصُمْنَا وَ رَزَقَنَا فَأَفْطَرْنَا اللَّهُمَّ تَقَبَّلْ مِنَّا وَ أَعِنَّا عَلَيْهِ وَ سَلِّمْنَا فِيهِ وَ تَسَلَّمْهُ مِنَّا فِي يُسْرٍ مِنْكَ وَ عَافِيَةٍ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي قَضَى عَنَّا يَوْماً مِنْ شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ .

O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Accept from us, and Aid us upon it, and Secure us in it, and Receive is from us in ease from You<sup>azwj</sup> and good health. The Praise is for Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, Who Accomplished for us one day from the Month of Ramazan’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول وربما يعد حسن ا - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (6/261)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Sayf Bin Ameyra, from Hassan Bin Mukhtar who said, ‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘What is the continuation regarding the Fasting?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘There is neither a continuation (without breaking Fast) regarding the Fasting, nor a silence for the day up to the night, nor an emancipation before ownership’.

citation.arabic_text: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) مَا الْوِصَالُ فِي الصِّيَامِ قَالَ فَقَالَ إِنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) قَالَ لَا وِصَالَ فِي صِيَامٍ وَ لَا صَمْتَ يَوْمٍ إِلَى اللَّيْلِ وَ لَا عِتْقَ قَبْلَ مِلْكٍ .

text: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Al Halby, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said; ‘The continuation regarding the Fasting is that he makes his dinner as his pre-dawn meal’.

citation.arabic_text: الْوِصَالُ فِي الصِّيَامِ أَنْ يَجْعَلَ عَشَاءَهُ سَحُورَهُ .
citation.translation: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Al Halby, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said; ‘The continuation regarding the Fasting is that he makes his dinner as his pre-dawn meal’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (16/261)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fal Bin Shazan, altogether from Ibn Abu Umery, from Hafs Bin Al Bakhtary, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The continuous regarding the Fasting is that one Fasts a day and a night, and breaks Fast in the pre-dawn meal’.

citation.arabic_text: الْمُوَاصِلُ فِي الصِّيَامِ يَصُومُ يَوْماً وَ لَيْلَةً وَ يُفْطِرُ فِي السَّحَرِ .

citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن لا يقصر عن الصحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (16/262)

text: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Washa, from Aban, from Zurara who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about Fasting the whole time, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is not Revealed. We<sup>asws</sup> dislike it’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنْ صَوْمِ الدَّهْرِ فَقَالَ لَمْ نَزَلْ نَكْرَهُهُ .

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having been asked about a man who partook a pre-dawn meal, then went out from his house, and the dawn had emerged and it was clear. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He should complete that Fast of his, then let him make up for it. So, if he had taken the pre-dawn meal during other than a Month of Ramazan after the dawn, so he should break’. Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘My<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> was Praying one night, and I<sup>asws</sup> ate. So he<sup>asws</sup> completed and said: ‘As for Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> has eaten and drunk after the dawn’. So he<sup>asws</sup> instructed me<sup>asws</sup>, so I<sup>asws</sup> broke the Fast of that day (which was) other than the Month of Ramazan’.

text: Muhammad Bin yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at Bin Mihran who said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a man who eats and drinks after the emergence of the dawn during a Month of Ramazan. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If it was such that he stood and looked (outside for the dawn), but did not see the dawn, so he ate, then returned, so he saw the dawn, so let him complete his Fast, and there is no repeating upon him; but if it was such that he stood up and ate and drank, then looked to the dawn, so he saw that the dawn had emerged, so let him complete his Fast, and he should compensate for it another day, because he began with the eating before looking, so upon him is the repeating’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ أَكَلَ وَ شَرِبَ بَعْدَ مَا طَلَعَ الْفَجْرُ فِي شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ فَقَالَ إِنْ كَانَ قَامَ فَنَظَرَ فَلَمْ يَرَ الْفَجْرَ فَأَكَلَ ثُمَّ عَادَ فَرَأَى الْفَجْرَ فَلْيُتِمَّ صَوْمَهُ وَ لَا إِعَادَةَ عَلَيْهِ وَ إِنْ كَانَ قَامَ فَأَكَلَ وَ شَرِبَ ثُمَّ نَظَرَ إِلَى الْفَجْرِ فَرَأَى أَنَّهُ قَدْ طَلَعَ الْفَجْرُ فَلْيُتِمَّ صَوْمَهُ وَ يَقْضِي يَوْماً آخَرَ لِأَنَّهُ بَدَأَ بِالْأَكْلِ قَبْلَ النَّظَرِ فَعَلَيْهِ الْإِعَادَةُ .

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya Bin Ammar who said, ‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘I instructed the maid that she looks whether the dawn has emerged or not, So she was saying, ‘It has not emerged’. text: Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin ShAzan, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Ays Bin Al Qasim who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about a man who goes out during the Month of Ramazan, and his companions are partaking their pre-dawn meal in the house. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He should complete his Fast, and he should make up for it’.

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Al Husayn Bin saeed, from Al Qasim Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ibrahim<sup>asws</sup> (7<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>), said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a man who drinks during the Month of Ramazan after the emergence of the dawn and he does not know’. text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at Bin Mihran who said, ‘I asked himasws about two men who stand to look at the dawn. So, one of the two says, ‘It is that’, and the other one says, ‘I do not see a thing’. Heasws said: ‘So, let him eat, the one for whom the dawn had not been evident, and it is forbidden (to eat) upon the one who claimed that he had seen the dawn. Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic is Saying [2:187] and eat and drink until the white thread becomes distinct from the black thread at Dawn’.

text: Muhammad Bin yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Al A’ala Bin Razeyn, from Musa Bin Bakr, from Zurara, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Ibn Am Maktoum recited the Azan for the morning Prayer, and a man passed by Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, and he<sup>saww</sup> was partaking a pre-dawn meal. So he<sup>saww</sup> invited him that he eats with him, but he said, ‘O Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>! The Muezzin has called the Azan for the dawn’. So he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘This is Ibn Am Maktoum, and he is reciting Azan at night. However, when Bilal recites Azan, so during that, you refrain’.

citation.arabic_text: أَذَّنَ ابْنُ أُمِّ مَكْتُومٍ لِصَلَاةِ الْغَدَاةِ وَ مَرَّ رَجُلٌ بِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) وَ هُوَ يَتَسَحَّرُ فَدَعَاهُ أَنْ يَأْكُلَ مَعَهُ فَقَالَ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ قَدْ أَذَّنَ الْمُؤَذِّنُ لِلْفَجْرِ فَقَالَ إِنَّ هَذَا ابْنُ أُمِّ مَكْتُومٍ وَ هُوَ يُؤَذِّنُ بِلَيْلٍ فَإِذَا أَذَّنَ بِلَالٌ فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ فَأَمْسِكْ .

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali Bin Atiyya, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The dawn, it is which, when you see it unobstructed, it is as if it is a white edge’.

citation.arabic_text: الْفَجْرُ هُوَ الَّذِي إِذَا رَأَيْتَهُ مُعْتَرِضاً كَأَنَّهُ بَيَاضُ سُورَى .

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, altogether from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the (distinction of the) white thread from the black thread. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: (It is) the whiteness of the day from the blackness of the night’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Bilal used to call the Azan for the Prophet<sup>saww</sup>, and Ibn Am Maktoum, and he was blind, would call the Azan at night, and Bilal would call the Azan when the dawn emerged. text: Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin ShAzan, and Ahmad Bin Idrees, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, altogether from Safwan Bin yahya, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, (It has been narrated) from one of the two (5th or 6th Imamasws) regarding the Words of Allahazwj the Exalted [2:187] It is made lawful to you to go to your wives on the night of the Fast – the Verse. Heasws said: ‘It was Revealed regarding Khawwat Bin Jubeyr Al-Ansary, and he was with the Prophetsaww during the (battle of) Khandaq, and he was Fasting. So evening came and he was upon that state, and it was such that before the Revelation of this Verse, whenever one of them fell asleep, the food and drink was Prohibited upon him. So Khawwat went over to his family when it was evening, so he said, ‘Is there anything (to eat) with you?’ So they said, ‘No, do not sleep until we prepare the food for you’. So he reclined and fell asleep. So they said to him, you have done it (fell asleep)?’ He said, ‘Yes’. So he spent the night upon that state (hungry and thirsty). So, in the morning, he went over to the ditch, and fainting overcame him. So, Rasool-Allahsaww passed by him. So when hesaww saw that which was with him, he informed him of how his matter was. So Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Sent down the Verse regarding him [2:187] and eat and drink until the white thread becomes distinct from the black thread at Dawn’.

citation.arabic_text: اللَّهِ تَعَالَى أُحِلَّ لَكُمْ لَيْلَةَ الصِّيامِ الرَّفَثُ إِلى نِسائِكُمْ الْآيَةَ فَقَالَ نَزَلَتْ فِي خَوَّاتِ بْنِ جُبَيْرٍ الْأَنْصَارِيِّ وَ كَانَ مَعَ النَّبِيِّ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) فِي الْخَنْدَقِ وَ هُوَ صَائِمٌ فَأَمْسَى وَ هُوَ عَلَى تِلْكَ الْحَالِ وَ كَانُوا قَبْلَ أَنْ تَنْزِلَ هَذِهِ الْآيَةُ إِذَا نَامَ أَحَدُهُمْ حُرِّمَ عَلَيْهِ الطَّعَامُ وَ الشَّرَابُ فَجَاءَ خَوَّاتٌ إِلَى أَهْلِهِ حِينَ أَمْسَى فَقَالَ هَلْ عِنْدَكُمْ طَعَامٌ فَقَالُوا لَا لَا تَنَمْ حَتَّى نُصْلِحَ لَكَ طَعَاماً فَاتَّكَأَ فَنَامَ فَقَالُوا لَهُ قَدْ فَعَلْتَ قَالَ نَعَمْ فَبَاتَ عَلَى تِلْكَ الْحَالِ فَأَصْبَحَ ثُمَّ غَدَا إِلَى الْخَنْدَقِ فَجَعَلَ يُغْشَى عَلَيْهِ فَمَرَّ بِهِ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) فَلَمَّا رَأَى الَّذِي بِهِ أَخْبَرَهُ كَيْفَ كَانَ أَمْرُهُ فَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ فِيهِ الْآيَةَ وَ كُلُوا وَ اشْرَبُوا حَتَّى يَتَبَيَّنَ لَكُمُ الْخَيْطُ الْأَبْيَضُ مِنَ الْخَيْطِ الْأَسْوَدِ مِنَ الْفَجْرِ
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin ShAzan, and Ahmad Bin Idrees, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, altogether from Safwan Bin yahya, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, (It has been narrated) from one of the two (5th or 6th Imamasws) regarding the Words of Allahazwj the Exalted [2:187] It is made lawful to you to go to your wives on the night of the Fast – the Verse. Heasws said: ‘It was Revealed regarding Khawwat Bin Jubeyr Al-Ansary, and he was with the Prophetsaww during the (battle of) Khandaq, and he was Fasting. So evening came and he was upon that state, and it was such that before the Revelation of this Verse, whenever one of them fell asleep, the food and drink was Prohibited upon him. So Khawwat went over to his family when it was evening, so he said, ‘Is there anything (to eat) with you?’ So they said, ‘No, do not sleep until we prepare the food for you’. So he reclined and fell asleep. So they said to him, you have done it (fell asleep)?’ He said, ‘Yes’. So he spent the night upon that state (hungry and thirsty). So, in the morning, he went over to the ditch, and fainting overcame him. So, Rasool-Allahsaww passed by him. So when hesaww saw that which was with him, he informed him of how his matter was. So Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Sent down the Verse regarding him [2:187] and eat and drink until the white thread becomes distinct from the black thread at Dawn’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (6/266)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al hakam, from Aasim Bin Humeyd, from Abu Baseer who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, so I said, ‘When does the food and drink become Prohibited upon the Fasting one and the Prayer becomes Permissible, the Dawn Prayer?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When the dawn presents itself, it would be like the white Coptic fabric, so from then the food becomes Prohibited, and the Fast opens, and the Prayer becomes Permissible, the Dawn Prayer’. I said, ‘So we are not with time until the emergence of the rays of the sun?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Far be it! Where are you going? That is the Prayer of the children’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) فَقُلْتُ مَتَى يَحْرُمُ الطَّعَامُ وَ الشَّرَابُ عَلَى الصَّائِمِ وَ تَحِلُّ الصَّلَاةُ صَلَاةُ الْفَجْرِ فَقَالَ إِذَا اعْتَرَضَ الْفَجْرُ وَ كَانَ كَالْقُبْطِيَّةِ الْبَيْضَاءِ فَثَمَّ يَحْرُمُ الطَّعَامُ وَ يَحِلُّ الصِّيَامُ وَ تَحِلُّ الصَّلَاةُ صَلَاةُ الْفَجْرِ قُلْتُ فَلَسْنَا فِي وَقْتٍ إِلَى أَنْ يَطْلُعَ شُعَاعُ الشَّمْسِ فَقَالَ هَيْهَاتَ أَيْنَ تَذْهَبُ تِلْكَ صَلَاةُ الصِّبْيَانِ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al hakam, from Aasim Bin Humeyd, from Abu Baseer who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, so I said, ‘When does the food and drink become Prohibited upon the Fasting one and the Prayer becomes Permissible, the Dawn Prayer?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When the dawn presents itself, it would be like the white Coptic fabric, so from then the food becomes Prohibited, and the Fast opens, and the Prayer becomes Permissible, the Dawn Prayer’. I said, ‘So we are not with time until the emergence of the rays of the sun?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Far be it! Where are you going? That is the Prayer of the children’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (6/267)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at who said, ‘I asked himasws about the people who are Fasting the Month of Ramazan, so the black cloud overcomes them during the setting of the sun. So they think that it is night, so they break Fast. Then the clouds move away, so the sun is (still) there’. So heasws said: ‘It is upon those that break the Fast, the (making up for) the Fast of that day. Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic is Saying [2:187] complete the Fast till night. So the one who eats before the entry of the night, so upon him is its making up, because he ate deliberately’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ قَوْمٍ صَامُوا شَهْرَ رَمَضَانَ فَغَشِيَهُمْ سَحَابٌ أَسْوَدُ عِنْدَ غُرُوبِ الشَّمْسِ فَظَنُّوا أَنَّهُ لَيْلٌ فَأَفْطَرُوا ثُمَّ إِنَّ السَّحَابَ انْجَلَى فَإِذَا الشَّمْسُ فَقَالَ عَلَى الَّذِي أَفْطَرَ صِيَامُ ذَلِكَ الْيَوْمِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ يَقُولُ أَتِمُّوا الصِّيامَ إِلَى اللَّيْلِ فَمَنْ أَكَلَ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَدْخُلَ اللَّيْلُ فَعَلَيْهِ قَضَاؤُهُ لِأَنَّهُ أَكَلَ مُتَعَمِّداً .

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa Bin Ubeyd, from Yunus, from Abu Baseer and Sama’at, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws regarding a group of people who are Fasting the Month of Ramazan, so the black cloud overcomes them during the setting of the sun. So they see it as being night, and some of them break the Fast. Then the clouds move away, so the sun is (still) there. Heasws said: ‘It is upon those who break (to make up for) the Fast of that day. Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic is Saying [2:187] complete the Fast till night. So the one who eats before the entry of the night, so upon him is its making up, because he ate deliberately’.

citation.arabic_text: قَوْمٍ صَامُوا شَهْرَ رَمَضَانَ فَغَشِيَهُمْ سَحَابٌ أَسْوَدُ عِنْدَ غُرُوبِ الشَّمْسِ فَرَأَوْا أَنَّهُ اللَّيْلُ فَأَفْطَرَ بَعْضُهُمْ ثُمَّ إِنَّ السَّحَابَ انْجَلَى فَإِذَا الشَّمْسُ قَالَ عَلَى الَّذِي أَفْطَرَ صِيَامُ ذَلِكَ الْيَوْمِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ يَقُولُ أَتِمُّوا الصِّيامَ إِلَى اللَّيْلِ فَمَنْ أَكَلَ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَدْخُلَ اللَّيْلُ فَعَلَيْهِ قَضَاؤُهُ لِأَنَّهُ أَكَلَ مُتَعَمِّداً .

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Isa Bin Ubeyd, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from the one who mentioned it, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The time of the fall of the disc (sun) and the Obligation of breaking from the Fasts is that, one stands facing the Qiblah and inspects the redness which rises from the east. So when it passes overhead towards the direction of the west, so the breaking of the Fast is Obligated, and the disc falls (sun sets)’.

citation.arabic_text: وَقْتُ سُقُوطِ الْقُرْصِ وَ وُجُوبِ الْإِفْطَارِ مِنَ الصِّيَامِ أَنْ يَقُومَ بِحِذَاءِ الْقِبْلَةِ وَ يَتَفَقَّدَ الْحُمْرَةَ الَّتِي تَرْتَفِعُ مِنَ الْمَشْرِقِ فَإِذَا جَازَتْ قِمَّةَ الرَّأْسِ إِلَى نَاحِيَةِ الْمَغْرِبِ فَقَدْ وَجَبَ الْإِفْطَارُ وَ سَقَطَ الْقُرْصُ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Isa Bin Ubeyd, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from the one who mentioned it, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The time of the fall of the disc (sun) and the Obligation of breaking from the Fasts is that, one stands facing the Qiblah and inspects the redness which rises from the east. So when it passes overhead towards the direction of the west, so the breaking of the Fast is Obligated, and the disc falls (sun sets)’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (16/270)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and a number of our companions, from Ahmad Bi Muhammad, altogether from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Al Qasim Ibn Urwat, from Bureyd Bin MUawiya who said, ‘I heard Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘When the redness disappears from this side, meaning the direction of the east, so the sun has disappeared in the east of the earth and its west’.

citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ إِذَا غَابَتِ الْحُمْرَةُ مِنْ هَذَا الْجَانِبِ يَعْنِي نَاحِيَةَ الْمَشْرِقِ فَقَدْ غَابَتِ الشَّمْسُ فِي شَرْقِ الْأَرْضِ وَ غَرْبِهَا .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and a number of our companions, from Ahmad Bi Muhammad, altogether from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Al Qasim Ibn Urwat, from Bureyd Bin MUawiya who said, ‘I heard Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘When the redness disappears from this side, meaning the direction of the east, so the sun has disappeared in the east of the earth and its west’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (16/270)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘He<sup>asws</sup> was asked about the breaking of the Fast before the Prayer or after it. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If it was such that with him are a group of people, he is fearing withholding them from their dinner, so let him break Fast along with them, but if it was other than that, so let him Pray, and let him break the Fast (after offering Salaat)’.

citation.arabic_text: سُئِلَ عَنِ الْإِفْطَارِ قَبْلَ الصَّلَاةِ أَوْ بَعْدَهَا قَالَ إِنْ كَانَ مَعَهُ قَوْمٌ يَخْشَى أَنْ يَحْبِسَهُمْ عَنْ عَشَائِهِمْ فَلْيُفْطِرْ مَعَهُمْ وَ إِنْ كَانَ غَيْرُ ذَلِكَ فَلْيُصَلِّ وَ لْيُفْطِرْ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘He<sup>asws</sup> was asked about the breaking of the Fast before the Prayer or after it. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If it was such that with him are a group of people, he is fearing withholding them from their dinner, so let him break Fast along with them, but if it was other than that, so let him Pray, and let him break the Fast (after offering Salaat)’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (16/270)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, altogether from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad Bin Usman, from Al Halby, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having been asked about a man who forgot, so he ate and drank, then remembered. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He should not break the Fast. But rather, it is something Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Graced him, so let him complete his Fast’.

citation.arabic_text: لَا يُفْطِرْ إِنَّمَا هُوَ شَيْ‏ءٌ رَزَقَهُ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ فَلْيُتِمَّ صَوْمَهُ .

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at who said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a man who Fasts in the Month of Ramazan, so he eats and drinks out of forgetfulness. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Let him complete his Fast, and there is not making up for it upon him’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ صَامَ فِي شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ فَأَكَلَ وَ شَرِبَ نَاسِياً قَالَ يُتِمُّ صَوْمَهُ وَ لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ قَضَاؤُهُ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at who said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a man who Fasts in the Month of Ramazan, so he eats and drinks out of forgetfulness. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Let him complete his Fast, and there is not making up for it upon him’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (16/271)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Dawood Bin Sirham, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding the man who forgets, so he eats during the Month of Ramazan. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He should complete his Fast. So, rather, it is something which Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has Fed it to him’.

citation.arabic_text: الرَّجُلِ يَنْسَى فَيَأْكُلُ فِي شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ قَالَ يُتِمُّ صَوْمَهُ فَإِنَّمَا هُوَ شَيْ‏ءٌ أَطْعَمَهُ اللَّهُ إِيَّاهُ .

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding a man who breaks a Fast from the Month of Ramazan deliberately for one day, without an excuse. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He should either emancipate a person, or Fasts two months consecutively, or feed sixty poor ones. So if he is not able, he should give in charity with whatever he can afford to’.

citation.arabic_text: رَجُلٍ أَفْطَرَ مِنْ شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ مُتَعَمِّداً يَوْماً وَاحِداً مِنْ غَيْرِ عُذْرٍ قَالَ يُعْتِقُ نَسَمَةً أَوْ يَصُومُ شَهْرَيْنِ مُتَتَابِعَيْنِ أَوْ يُطْعِمُ سِتِّينَ مِسْكِيناً فَإِنْ لَمْ يَقْدِرْ تَصَدَّقَ بِمَا يُطِيقُ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding a man who breaks a Fast from the Month of Ramazan deliberately for one day, without an excuse. text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin ShAzan, altogether from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel Bin Darraj, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having been asked about a man who breaks a Fast for a day from the Month of Ramazan, deliberately. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘A man came over to the Prophet<sup>saww</sup>, so he said, ‘I am destroyed, O Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>!’ So he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘What is the matter?’ So he said, ‘The Fire, O Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>!’ He<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘And what is the matter?’ He said, ‘I fell upon my wife’. He<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Give in charity and seek Forgiveness’. So the man said, ‘By the One<sup>azwj</sup> Who Magnified your<sup>saww</sup> rights, nothing is left in the house, neither less nor more’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘A man from the people came over with a sack of dates in which were twenty Sa’as (a unit of measurement), which happens to be ten Sa’as by (the measurement) of our Sa’as’. So Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said to him: ‘Take these dates and give in charity with it’. So he said, ‘O Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>! Whom shall I give it in charity with it, and I have informed you<sup>saww</sup> that there is neither in my house anything less nor more?’ He<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘So take it and feed it to your dependents and seek Forgiveness of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’. He (the narrator) said, ‘So when we came out, our companions said, ‘It has to be begun with the emancipation’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Emancipate, or Fast, or charity’.

citation.arabic_text: سُئِلَ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ ( عليه السلام ) عَنْ رَجُلٍ شَهِدَ عَلَيْهِ شُهُودٌ أَنَّهُ أَفْطَرَ مِنْ شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ ثَلَاثَةَ أَيَّامٍ قَالَ يُسْأَلُ هَلْ عَلَيْكَ فِي إِفْطَارِكَ فِي شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ إِثْمٌ فَإِنْ قَالَ لَا فَإِنَّ عَلَى الْإِمَامِ أَنْ يَقْتُلَهُ وَ إِنْ قَالَ نَعَمْ فَإِنَّ عَلَى الْإِمَامِ أَنْ يَنْهَكَهُ ضَرْباً .

text: Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Bundar, from Ibrahim Bin Is’haq Al Ahmar, from Abdullah Bin Hammad, from Al Mufazzal Bin Umar, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws regarding a man who went to his wife and he was Fasting and she was Fasting. So heasws said: ‘If it was such that she had disliked it, so upon him would be two expiations; and if it was such that she was willing, so upon him would be an expiation and upon her would be an expiation; and if it was such that he had coerced her, so upon him would be the whipping of fifty lashes, being half the Legal Penaly (Hadd); and if it was that she was willing, he would be whipped twenty five lashes, and she would be whipped twenty five lashes’.

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Dawood Bin Al No’man, from Mansour Bin Hazim who said, ‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘What are you<sup>asws</sup> saying regarding the Fasting one who kisses the slave girl and the wife?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘As for the old man like me<sup>asws</sup> and like you, so there is no problem, and as for the young man, so no, because he would not be safe, and the kissing is one of the two lustful desires’. I said, ‘So what is your<sup>asws</sup> view regarding the likes of me who happens to have the slave girl for him, so he plays with her?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Do you need it, O Abu Hazim? How is your food intake?’ I said, ‘If I am satiated, it harms me, and if I am hungry, it weakens me’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> am like that. So, how are you and the women?’ I said, ‘And there is nothing’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘But I<sup>asws</sup>, O Abu Hazim, whatever I<sup>asws</sup> so desire to, that happens from me<sup>asws</sup>, until I<sup>asws</sup> do it’.

citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, altogether from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdllah<sup>asws</sup> having said regarding a man who bed-wets at the beginning of the night, or attains from his wife, then he sleeps deliberately during the Month of Ramazan, until the morning. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He should complete that Fast of his, then he should make up for it, when he broke a Fast from the Month of Ramazan, and he should seek Forgiveness of his Lord<sup>azwj</sup>’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (6/278)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Al A’ala Bin Razeyn, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, (It has been narrated) from one of the two (5<sup>th</sup> or 6<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>), said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the man who touches the slave girl during the Month of Ramazan, then he sleeps before he washes. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He should complete his Fast and he should make up for the Fast of that day, except if he wakes up before the emergence of the dawn. So if he waits for the water to warm up, or to be drawn, so the dawn emerges, then there is no making up for (the Fast of) his day’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يُصِيبُ الْجَارِيَةَ فِي شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ ثُمَّ يَنَامُ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَغْتَسِلَ قَالَ يُتِمُّ صَوْمَهُ وَ يَقْضِي ذَلِكَ الْيَوْمَ إِلَّا أَنْ يَسْتَيْقِظَ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَطْلُعَ الْفَجْرُ فَإِنِ انْتَظَرَ مَاءً يُسَخَّنُ أَوْ يَسْتَقِي فَطَلَعَ الْفَجْرُ فَلَا يَقْضِي يَوْمَهُ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Al A’ala Bin Razeyn, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, (It has been narrated) from one of the two (5<sup>th</sup> or 6<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>), said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the man who touches the slave girl during the Month of Ramazan, then he sleeps before he washes. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He should complete his Fast and he should make up for the Fast of that day, except if he wakes up before the emergence of the dawn. So if he waits for the water to warm up, or to be drawn, so the dawn emerges, then there is no making up for (the Fast of) his day’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (6/279)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukeyr who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the man comes to be with sexual impurity, then he sleeps until the morning. Can he Fast that day voluntarily?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Is he not with the choice what is between him and what is between half the day?’ He (the narrator) said, ‘And I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the man who bed wets during the day in the Month of Ramazan, he complete his Fast just as he is.’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يُجْنِبُ ثُمَّ يَنَامُ حَتَّى يُصْبِحَ أَ يَصُومُ ذَلِكَ الْيَوْمَ تَطَوُّعاً فَقَالَ أَ لَيْسَ هُوَ بِالْخِيَارِ مَا بَيْنَهُ وَ بَيْنَ نِصْفِ النَّهَارِ قَالَ وَ سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يَحْتَلِمُ بِالنَّهَارِ فِي شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ يُتِمُّ صَوْمَهُ كَمَا هُوَ فَقَالَ لَا بَأْسَ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukeyr who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the man comes to be with sexual impurity, then he sleeps until the morning. Can he Fast that day voluntarily?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Is he not with the choice what is between him and what is between half the day?’ He (the narrator) said, ‘And I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the man who bed wets during the day in the Month of Ramazan, he complete his Fast just as he is.’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق كالصحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (6/279)

text: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hajjal, from Ibn Sinan who said, ‘My father wrote to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, and he was making up for the (Fast of the) Month of Ramazan, and said, ‘I woke up in the morning with the washing, the sexual impurity hit me, so I did not wash until the emergence of the dawn’. So he<sup>asws</sup> answered him: ‘Do not Fast this day, and Fast the next day’.

citation.arabic_text: كَتَبَ أَبِي إِلَى أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) وَ كَانَ يَقْضِي شَهْرَ رَمَضَانَ وَ قَالَ إِنِّي أَصْبَحْتُ بِالْغُسْلِ وَ أَصَابَتْنِي جَنَابَةٌ فَلَمْ أَغْتَسِلْ حَتَّى طَلَعَ الْفَجْرُ فَأَجَابَهُ ( عليه السلام ) لَا تَصُمْ هَذَا الْيَوْمَ وَ صُمْ غَداً .
citation.translation: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hajjal, from Ibn Sinan who said, ‘My father wrote to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, and he was making up for the (Fast of the) Month of Ramazan, and said, ‘I woke up in the morning with the washing, the sexual impurity hit me, so I did not wash until the emergence of the dawn’. So he<sup>asws</sup> answered him: ‘Do not Fast this day, and Fast the next day’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (16/279)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Ali Bin Raib, from Ibrahim, Bin Maymoun who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the man who came to be with sexual impurity at night during the Month of Ramazan, so he forgot that he should be washing until that week was past, or he came out from the Month of Ramazan. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Upon him is the making up for the Prayer and the Fast’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يُجْنِبُ بِاللَّيْلِ فِي شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ فَنَسِيَ أَنْ يَغْتَسِلَ حَتَّى يَمْضِيَ بِذَلِكَ جُمْعَةٌ أَوْ يَخْرُجَ شَهْرُ رَمَضَانَ قَالَ عَلَيْهِ قَضَاءُ الصَّلَاةِ وَ الصَّوْمِ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Ali Bin Raib, from Ibrahim, Bin Maymoun who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the man who came to be with sexual impurity at night during the Month of Ramazan, so he forgot that he should be washing until that week was past, or he came out from the Month of Ramazan. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Upon him is the making up for the Prayer and the Fast’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (6/280)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The Fasting-one can stay still in the water, and (but) he cannot immerse his head into the water’.

citation.arabic_text: الصَّائِمُ يَسْتَنْقِعُ فِي الْمَاءِ وَ لَا يَرْتَمِسُ رَأْسُهُ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The Fasting-one can stay still in the water, and (but) he cannot immerse his head into the water’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (16/281)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hareyz, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Neither can the Fasting one nor one in Ihraam can immerse his head into the water’.

citation.arabic_text: لَا يَرْتَمِسُ الصَّائِمُ وَ لَا الْمُحْرِمُ رَأْسُهُ فِي الْمَاءِ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hareyz, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Neither can the Fasting one nor one in Ihraam can immerse his head into the water’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (16/282)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Al A’ala Bin Razeyn, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The Fasting one can stay still in the water and he can pour water upon his head, and he can cool himself with the (wet) clothes, and he can sprinkle (cool himself) with the ventilator, and he can sprinkle (cool himself) with the blower beneath him, but he cannot immerse his head into the water (to cool himself)’.

citation.arabic_text: الصَّائِمُ يَسْتَنْقِعُ فِي الْمَاءِ وَ يَصُبُّ عَلَى رَأْسِهِ وَ يَتَبَرَّدُ بِالثَّوْبِ وَ يَنْضَحُ بِالْمِرْوَحَةِ وَ يَنْضَحُ الْبُورِيَاءَ تَحْتَهُ وَ لَا يَغْمِسُ رَأْسَهُ فِي الْمَاءِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Al A’ala Bin Razeyn, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The Fasting one can stay still in the water and he can pour water upon his head, and he can cool himself with the (wet) clothes, and he can sprinkle (cool himself) with the ventilator, and he can sprinkle (cool himself) with the blower beneath him, but he cannot immerse his head into the water (to cool himself)’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (6/282)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Musa Bin Sa’dan, from Abdullah Bin Al Haysam, from Abdullah Bin Sinan who said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Do not attach clothes upon your body while they are wet, and you are Fasting, until your wring them (first)’.

citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ لَا تُلْزِقْ ثَوْبَكَ إِلَى جَسَدِكَ وَ هُوَ رَطْبٌ وَ أَنْتَ صَائِمٌ حَتَّى تَعْصِرَهُ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Musa Bin Sa’dan, from Abdullah Bin Al Haysam, from Abdullah Bin Sinan who said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Do not attach clothes upon your body while they are wet, and you are Fasting, until your wring them (first)’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (6/282)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, and someone else from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Al Sayyari, from Muhammad Bin Ali Al Hamdany, from Hanan Bin Sadeyr who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the Fasting one staying still in the water. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem, but he should not immerse himself into it; and the woman should neither stay still in the water because she would carry the water with her private part’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنِ الصَّائِمِ يَسْتَنْقِعُ فِي الْمَاءِ قَالَ لَا بَأْسَ وَ لَكِنْ لَا يَنْغَمِسُ فِيهِ وَ الْمَرْأَةُ لَا تَسْتَنْقِعُ فِي الْمَاءِ لِأَنَّهَا تَحْمِلُ الْمَاءَ بِفَرْجِهَا .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, and someone else from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Al Sayyari, from Muhammad Bin Ali Al Hamdany, from Hanan Bin Sadeyr who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the Fasting one staying still in the water. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem, but he should not immerse himself into it; and the woman should neither stay still in the water because she would carry the water with her private part’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (16/282)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from one of his companions, from Musna Al Hannat and Al Hassan Al Sayqal who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the Fasting one immersing himself into the water. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No, and neither can the one in Ihraam’. He (the narrator) said, ‘And I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the Fasting one wearing the dripping wet clothes. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنِ الصَّائِمِ يَرْتَمِسُ فِي الْمَاءِ قَالَ لَا وَ لَا الْمُحْرِمُ قَالَ وَ سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ الصَّائِمِ يَلْبَسُ الثَّوْبَ الْمَبْلُولَ قَالَ لَا .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from one of his companions, from Musna Al Hannat and Al Hassan Al Sayqal who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the Fasting one immersing himself into the water. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No, and neither can the one in Ihraam’. He (the narrator) said, ‘And I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the Fasting one wearing the dripping wet clothes. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (16/283)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding the Fasting one performing ablution for the Prayer, so the water enters into his throat. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If his ablution was for the Obligatory Prayer, so there is nothing upon him, but if his ablution was for an optional Prayer, so upon him is the making up for it’.

citation.arabic_text: الصَّائِمِ يَتَوَضَّأُ لِلصَّلَاةِ فَيَدْخُلُ الْمَاءُ حَلْقَهُ فَقَالَ إِنْ كَانَ وُضُوؤُهُ لِصَلَاةِ فَرِيضَةٍ فَلَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ شَيْ‏ءٌ وَ إِنْ كَانَ وُضُوؤُهُ لِصَلَاةِ نَافِلَةٍ فَعَلَيْهِ الْقَضَاءُ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding the Fasting one performing ablution for the Prayer, so the water enters into his throat. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If his ablution was for the Obligatory Prayer, so there is nothing upon him, but if his ablution was for an optional Prayer, so upon him is the making up for it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (16/283)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail Bin Marrar, from Yunus, from Abu Jameela, from Zayd, (It has been narrated) from Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding the Fasting one rinsing his mouth. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He should not swallow his saliva until he spits it out three times’.

citation.arabic_text: الصَّائِمِ يَتَمَضْمَضُ قَالَ لَا يَبْلَعْ رِيقَهُ حَتَّى يَبْزُقَ ثَلَاثَ مَرَّاتٍ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail Bin Marrar, from Yunus, from Abu Jameela, from Zayd, (It has been narrated) from Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding the Fasting one rinsing his mouth. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He should not swallow his saliva until he spits it out three times’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (16/284)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from the one who mentioned it, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding the Fasting one rinsing his mouth and inhaling. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, but he should not swallow’.

citation.arabic_text: الصَّائِمِ يَتَمَضْمَضُ وَ يَسْتَنْشِقُ قَالَ نَعَمْ وَ لَكِنْ لَا يُبَالِغْ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from the one who mentioned it, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding the Fasting one rinsing his mouth and inhaling. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, but he should not swallow’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (16/284)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Al Rayyan Bin Al Salt, from Yunus who said, ‘The Fasting one can brush his teeth whenever he so desires to, and if he rinses his mouth during a time of Obligatory Prayers, and the water enters into his throat, so there is nothing upon him, and he can complete his Fast; and if he were to rinse his mouth during a time other than that of an Obligatory Prayer, and the water enters into his throat, so upon him would be the repeating, and it is better for the Fasting one if he does not rinse his mouth’.

citation.arabic_text: الصَّائِمُ فِي شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ يَسْتَاكُ مَتَى شَاءَ وَ إِنْ تَمَضْمَضَ فِي وَقْتِ فَرِيضَتِهِ فَدَخَلَ الْمَاءُ حَلْقَهُ فَلَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ شَيْ‏ءٌ وَ قَدْ تَمَّ صَوْمُهُ وَ إِنْ تَمَضْمَضَ فِي غَيْرِ وَقْتِ فَرِيضَةٍ فَدَخَلَ الْمَاءُ حَلْقَهُ فَعَلَيْهِ الْإِعَادَةُ وَ الْأَفْضَلُ لِلصَّائِمِ أَنْ لَا يَتَمَضْمَضَ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Al Rayyan Bin Al Salt, from Yunus who said, ‘The Fasting one can brush his teeth whenever he so desires to, and if he rinses his mouth during a time of Obligatory Prayers, and the water enters into his throat, so there is nothing upon him, and he can complete his Fast; and if he were to rinse his mouth during a time other than that of an Obligatory Prayer, and the water enters into his throat, so upon him would be the repeating, and it is better for the Fasting one if he does not rinse his mouth’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (16/285)

text: Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin ShAzan and Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, altogether from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Ibn Muskam, from Al Halby, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘When the Fasting one vomits, so upon him would be the making up for that day, and if he nauseates from without vomiting, so let him complete his Fast’.

citation.arabic_text: إِذَا تَقَيَّأَ الصَّائِمُ فَعَلَيْهِ قَضَاءُ ذَلِكَ الْيَوْمِ وَ إِنْ ذَرَعَهُ مِنْ غَيْرِ أَنْ يَتَقَيَّأَ فَلْيُتِمَّ صَوْمَهُ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin ShAzan and Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, altogether from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Ibn Muskam, from Al Halby, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘When the Fasting one vomits, so upon him would be the making up for that day, and if he nauseates from without vomiting, so let him complete his Fast’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (16/285)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, altogether from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘When the Fasting-one vomits, so he has broken his Fast, and if he nauseates from without vomiting, so let him complete his Fast’.

citation.arabic_text: إِذَا تَقَيَّأَ الصَّائِمُ فَقَدْ أَفْطَرَ وَ إِنْ ذَرَعَهُ مِنْ غَيْرِ أَنْ يَتَقَيَّأَ فَلْيُتِمَّ صَوْمَهُ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, altogether from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘When the Fasting-one vomits, so he has broken his Fast, and if he nauseates from without vomiting, so let him complete his Fast’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (16/286)

text: Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin ShAzan, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding the one who nauseates to vomit (but does not), and he is Fasting. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Let him complete his Fast and the does not have to make up for it’.

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is not with anything’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يَخْرُجُ مِنْ جَوْفِهِ الْقَلْسُ حَتَّى يَبْلُغَ الْحَلْقَ ثُمَّ يَرْجِعُ إِلَى جَوْفِهِ وَ هُوَ صَائِمٌ قَالَ لَيْسَ بِشَيْ‏ءٍ .

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Al A’ala Bin Razeyn, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said, ‘Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> was asked about the regurgitation, would the Fasting one break his Fast?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No’.

citation.arabic_text: سُئِلَ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ ( عليه السلام ) عَنِ الْقَلْسِ يُفَطِّرُ الصَّائِمَ قَالَ لَا .

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at who said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the regurgitation, and it is the belching which raises the food from inside the man, from without it becoming a vomit, and he is standing during the Prayer. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘That would not break his ablution, nor would it cut off his Prayer, nor would it break his Fast’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ الْقَلْسِ وَ هِيَ الْجُشْأَةُ يَرْتَفِعُ الطَّعَامُ مِنْ جَوْفِ الرَّجُلِ مِنْ غَيْرِ أَنْ يَكُونَ تَقَيَّأَ وَ هُوَ قَائِمٌ فِي الصَّلَاةِ قَالَ لَا يَنْقُضُ ذَلِكَ وُضُوءَهُ وَ لَا يَقْطَعُ صَلَاتَهُ وَ لَا يُفَطِّرُ صِيَامَهُ.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, altogether from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the Fasting-one, can he get cupping done?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> fear upon him. Does he not fear upon himself?’ I said, ‘What is that which he should be fearing upon?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The fainting, or by it the bile would be stirred’. I said, ‘What is your<sup>asws</sup> view if he is strong upon that and he does not fear anything?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, if he so desires to’.

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Al Husayn Bin Abu Al A’ala who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the cupping for the Fasting one. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, when he does not fear weakness’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنِ الْحِجَامَةِ لِلصَّائِمِ قَالَ نَعَمْ إِذَا لَمْ يَخَفْ ضَعْفاً .

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Al A’ala Bin Razeyn, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having been asked about the man who enters the bathhouse and he is Fasting. citation.arabic_text: شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ فَقَالَ الصَّائِمُ لَا يَجُوزُ لَهُ أَنْ يَحْتَقِنَ .

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Al Amraky Bin Ali, (It has been narrated) from Ali son of Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, from his brother<sup>asws</sup> Musa<sup>asws</sup> Bin Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the man and the woman, is it correct for them that the medication is inserted into them and they are both Fasting?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said; ‘There is no problem’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ الرَّجُلِ وَ الْمَرْأَةِ هَلْ يَصْلُحُ لَهُمَا أَنْ يَسْتَدْخِلَا الدَّوَاءَ وَ هُمَا صَائِمَانِ قَالَ لَا بَأْسَ .

text: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Husayn, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from his father who said, ‘I wrote to Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, ‘What are you<sup>asws</sup> saying regarding the enema which the human being has inserted and he is Fasting’. citation.arabic_text: كَتَبْتُ إِلَى أَبِي الْحَسَنِ ( عليه السلام ) مَا تَقُولُ فِي التَّلَطُّفِ يَسْتَدْخِلُهُ الْإِنْسَانُ وَ هُوَ صَائِمٌ فَكَتَبَ لَا بَأْسَ بِالْجَامِدِ .

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Suleyman Al Fara’a, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’farasws regarding the Fasting-one who applies Kohl (in the eyes). Heasws said: ‘There is no problem with it. It is neither a food nor a drink’. Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Suleyman Al Fara’a, from someone else, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’farasws – similar to it.

citation.arabic_text: الصَّائِمِ يَكْتَحِلُ قَالَ لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ لَيْسَ بِطَعَامٍ وَ لَا شَرَابٍ . عَلِيُّ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ ابْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ الْفَرَّاءِ عَنْ غَيْرِ وَاحِدٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ ( عليه السلام ) مِثْلَهُ .

Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Suleyman Al Fara’a, from someone else, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’farasws – similar to it.

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Sa’ad Bin Saeed Al Ashary, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the one who is hit by conjunctivitis during the Month of Ramazan, can he sprinkle his eyes by the day and he is Fasting?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He can sprinkle when he breaks Fast but he cannot sprinkle it and he is Fasting’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُهُ عَمَّنْ يُصِيبُهُ الرَّمَدُ فِي شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ هَلْ يَذُرُّ عَيْنَهُ بِالنَّهَارِ وَ هُوَ صَائِمٌ قَالَ يَذُرُّهَا إِذَا أَفْطَرَ وَ لَا يَذُرُّهَا وَ هُوَ صَائِمٌ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Sa’ad Bin Saeed Al Ashary, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the one who is hit by conjunctivitis during the Month of Ramazan, can he sprinkle his eyes by the day and he is Fasting?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He can sprinkle when he breaks Fast but he cannot sprinkle it and he is Fasting’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (6/291)

So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When the Kohl was such that there is Musk in it, and there is no food to be in his throat, so there is no problem with it’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ الْكُحْلِ لِلصَّائِمِ فَقَالَ إِذَا كَانَ كُحْلًا لَيْسَ فِيهِ مِسْكٌ وَ لَيْسَ لَهُ طَعْمٌ فِي الْحَلْقِ فَلَا بَأْسَ بِهِ .

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Al Husayn Bin Abu Al A’ala who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the tooth-brushing. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, he can brush teeth whichever time of the day he so desires to’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنِ السِّوَاكِ لِلصَّائِمِ فَقَالَ نَعَمْ يَسْتَاكُ أَيَّ النَّهَارِ شَاءَ .

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the Fasting-one who brushes the teeth with the water. citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the Fasting-one who brushes the teeth with the water. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem with it’. And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He should not brush with the wet toothstick’.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah Bin Al Mugheira, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having disliked for the Fasting that he brushes with the wet tooth-stick, and said: ‘There is no harm if he dampens his tooth-stick with the water, then he shakes is until there does not remain anything in it’.

citation.arabic_text: لَا يَضُرُّ أَنْ يَبُلَّ سِوَاكَهُ بِالْمَاءِ ثُمَّ يَنْفُضَهُ حَتَّى لَا يَبْقَى فِيهِ شَيْ‏ءٌ .

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Giyas Bin Ibrahim, (It has been narrated) from Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, from his<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> that Ali<sup>asws</sup> disliked that the Musk be applied with by the Fasting one’.

citation.arabic_text: أَنَّ عَلِيّاً صَلَوَاتُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ كَرِهَ الْمِسْكَ أَنْ يَتَطَيَّبَ بِهِ الصَّائِمُ .

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Dawood Bin Is’haq Al Haza’a, from Muhammad Bin Al Fayz who said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> forbid from the daffodils. So I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! Why is that so?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Because it is an aroma of the non-Arabs’. And, one of our companions informed me that the non-Arabs used to smell it when they were Fasting, and said, ‘It restrains the hunger’.

citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) يَنْهَى عَنِ النَّرْجِسِ فَقُلْتُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ لِمَ ذَلِكَ فَقَالَ لِأَنَّهُ رَيْحَانُ الْأَعَاجِمِ وَ أَخْبَرَنِي بَعْضُ أَصْحَابِنَا أَنَّ الْأَعَاجِمَ كَانَتْ تَشَمُّهُ إِذَا صَامُوا وَ قَالُوا إِنَّهُ يُمْسِكُ الْجُوعَ .

And it is reported that he<sup>asws</sup> did not smell the aromas because it was disliked for him<sup>asws</sup> that he<sup>asws</sup> derive pleasure with it.

citation.arabic_text: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) الصَّائِمُ يَشَمُّ الرَّيْحَانَ وَ الطِّيبَ قَالَ لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ . وَ رُوِيَ أَنَّهُ لَا يَشَمُّ الرَّيْحَانَ لِأَنَّهُ يُكْرَهُ لَهُ أَنْ يَتَلَذَّذَ بِهِ .
