text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘The Fasting as an expiation for the oath regarding the Zihaar is of two consecutive months, and the ‘consecutive’ is that he Fasts a month and Fasts from the other month a few days, or something from it. So if something presents itself to him to break in it, he breaks. Then he makes up for what remains upon him. And if he Fasts a month, then something presents itself to him, so he breaks before he Fasts anything from the other (month), so he has not followed it. He has to repeat the Fasts, all of it’.

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at Bin Mihran who said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the man who happens to have the Fasting of two consecutive months upon him. Can he break in between the days?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When the Fasts are month than a month, so he connects it. Then a matter presents itself to him, so he breaks, then there is no problem. So if it was less than a month, or a month (exactly), so upon him is that he repeats the Fasts’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يَكُونُ عَلَيْهِ صَوْمُ شَهْرَيْنِ مُتَتَابِعَيْنِ أَ يُفَرِّقُ بَيْنَ الْأَيَّامِ فَقَالَ إِذَا صَامَ أَكْثَرَ مِنْ شَهْرٍ فَوَصَلَهُ ثُمَّ عَرَضَ لَهُ أَمْرٌ فَأَفْطَرَ فَلَا بَأْسَ فَإِنْ كَانَ أَقَلَّ مِنْ شَهْرٍ أَوْ شَهْراً فَعَلَيْهِ أَنْ يُعِيدَ الصِّيَامَ .

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws regarding a man who had the Fasts of two consecutive months upon him regardin Zihaar. So he Fasted Zil-Qaad. The Zil-Hajj entered upon him. Heasws said: ‘He can Fast Zil-Hijja, all of it, except for the days of Al-Tashreek (11th, 12th & 13th). He would make up for it during the beginning of Al-Muharram until he completes the three days. Thus, he would have Fasted two months consecutively’. Heasws said: ‘And it is not befitting for him that he approaches his wife until he has made up for the days of Al-Tashreek which he had not Fasted, and there is no problem if he were to Fast a month, then Fast a few days from the months which follows it. Then if a reason presents itself to him, he can cut it, then make up for it from afterwards to complete the two months’.

text: Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Mansour Bin Hazim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said regarding a man who Fasts Shaban regarding Zihaar, the he sees the Month of Ramazan, (Imamasws) said: ‘He should Fast Ramazaan, and he resumes the Fasting. So if he had Fasted regarding the Zihaar of an increase in the half by a day, he can make up for it for his remainder’.

citation.arabic_text: فِي رَجُلٍ صَامَ فِي ظِهَارٍ شَعْبَانَ ثُمَّ أَدْرَكَهُ شَهْرُ رَمَضَانَ قَالَ يَصُومُ رَمَضَانَ وَ يَسْتَأْنِفُ الصَّوْمَ فَإِنْ هُوَ صَامَ فِي الظِّهَارِ فَزَادَ فِي النِّصْفِ يَوْماً قَضَى بَقِيَّتَهُ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Mansour Bin Hazim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said regarding a man who Fasts Shaban regarding Zihaar, the he sees the Month of Ramazan, (Imamasws) said: ‘He should Fast Ramazaan, and he resumes the Fasting. So if he had Fasted regarding the Zihaar of an increase in the half by a day, he can make up for it for his remainder’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول كالصحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (6/347)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Musa Bin Bakr, from Al Fuzayl, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said regarding a man upon whom were Fasts of a month, so he Fasts fifteen days, then a matter presents itself, said: ‘If he had Fasted fifteen days, so for him it that he makes up for what remains, and even if it was less than fifteen days, it would not suffice for him until he Fasts a month completely’.

citation.arabic_text: فِي رَجُلٍ جَعَلَ عَلَيْهِ صَوْمَ شَهْرٍ فَصَامَ مِنْهُ خَمْسَةَ عَشَرَ يَوْماً ثُمَّ عَرَضَ لَهُ أَمْرٌ فَقَالَ إِنْ كَانَ صَامَ خَمْسَةَ عَشَرَ يَوْماً فَلَهُ أَنْ يَقْضِيَ مَا بَقِيَ وَ إِنْ كَانَ أَقَلَّ مِنْ خَمْسَةَ عَشَرَ يَوْماً لَمْ يُجْزِئْهُ حَتَّى يَصُومَ شَهْراً تَامّاً .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Musa Bin Bakr, from Al Fuzayl, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said regarding a man upon whom were Fasts of a month, so he Fasts fifteen days, then a matter presents itself, said: ‘If he had Fasted fifteen days, so for him it that he makes up for what remains, and even if it was less than fifteen days, it would not suffice for him until he Fasts a month completely’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (6/347)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Qasim Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about cutting a Fast of a expiation of the oath, and an expiation for the Zihaar, and an expiation for the killing, so heasws said: ‘If there were the Fasts of two consecutive months upon the man, so he beaks, or falls sick during the first month, so upon him would be that he repeats the Fasts. And if he had Fasted the first month, and Fasted something from the other month, then there presents to him what for him is an excuse therein, so upon him is that he makes up for it (the remainder)’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنْ قَطْعِ صَوْمِ كَفَّارَةِ الْيَمِينِ وَ كَفَّارَةِ الظِّهَارِ وَ كَفَّارَةِ الْقَتْلِ فَقَالَ إِنْ كَانَ عَلَى رَجُلٍ صِيَامُ شَهْرَيْنِ مُتَتَابِعَيْنِ فَأَفْطَرَ أَوْ مَرِضَ فِي الشَّهْرِ الْأَوَّلِ فَإِنَّ عَلَيْهِ أَنْ يُعِيدَ الصِّيَامَ وَ إِنْ صَامَ الشَّهْرَ الْأَوَّلَ وَ صَامَ مِنَ الشَّهْرِ الثَّانِي شَيْئاً ثُمَّ عَرَضَ لَهُ مَا لَهُ فِيهِ عُذْرٌ فَإِنَّ عَلَيْهِ أَنْ يَقْضِيَ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Qasim Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about cutting a Fast of a expiation of the oath, and an expiation for the Zihaar, and an expiation for the killing, so heasws said: ‘If there were the Fasts of two consecutive months upon the man, so he beaks, or falls sick during the first month, so upon him would be that he repeats the Fasts. And if he had Fasted the first month, and Fasted something from the other month, then there presents to him what for him is an excuse therein, so upon him is that he makes up for it (the remainder)’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (6/348)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Ali Bin Raib, from Zurara, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a man who kills a man in error during the Sacred Month. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The wergild is harsh upon him, and upon him is the emancipation (liberation) of a neck, or Fasting two months consecutively from the Sacred months’. I said, ‘Supposing something enters into this?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘What would it be?’ I said, ‘A day of Eid, and days of Al-Tashreek (11<sup>th</sup>, 12<sup>th</sup> and 13<sup>th</sup> of Zil-Hijja)?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He would Fast these, for it is a right necessitated upon him’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ قَتَلَ رَجُلًا خَطَأً فِي الشَّهْرِ الْحَرَامِ قَالَ تُغَلَّظُ عَلَيْهِ الدِّيَةُ وَ عَلَيْهِ عِتْقُ رَقَبَةٍ أَوْ صِيَامُ شَهْرَيْنِ مُتَتَابِعَيْنِ مِنْ أَشْهُرِ الْحُرُمِ قُلْتُ فَإِنَّهُ يَدْخُلُ فِي هَذَا شَيْ‏ءٌ فَقَالَ مَا هُوَ قُلْتُ يَوْمُ الْعِيدِ وَ أَيَّامُ التَّشْرِيقِ قَالَ يَصُومُهُ فَإِنَّهُ حَقٌّ يَلْزَمُهُ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Ali Bin Raib, from Zurara, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a man who kills a man in error during the Sacred Month. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The wergild is harsh upon him, and upon him is the emancipation (liberation) of a neck, or Fasting two months consecutively from the Sacred months’. I said, ‘Supposing something enters into this?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘What would it be?’ I said, ‘A day of Eid, and days of Al-Tashreek (11<sup>th</sup>, 12<sup>th</sup> and 13<sup>th</sup> of Zil-Hijja)?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He would Fast these, for it is a right necessitated upon him’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (16/348)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Aban Bin taghlub, from Zurara who said, ‘I said to Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, ‘A man kills a man in the Sanctuary’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Upon him is a wergild and a third, and he would Fast two months consecutively from the Sacred months, and he would emancipate (liberate) a neck, and he would feed sixty poor ones’. I said, ‘(Supposing) something enters into this?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And what would it be?’ I said, ‘The two Eids, and the days of Tashreek (11<sup>th</sup>, 12<sup>th</sup>, & 13<sup>th</sup> of Zil-Hijja)?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He would Fast it, for it is a right necessitated upon him’.

citation.arabic_text: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي جَعْفَرٍ ( عليه السلام ) رَجُلٌ قَتَلَ رَجُلًا فِي الْحَرَمِ قَالَ عَلَيْهِ دِيَةٌ وَ ثُلُثٌ وَ يَصُومُ شَهْرَيْنِ مُتَتَابِعَيْنِ مِنْ أَشْهُرِ الْحُرُمِ وَ يُعْتِقُ رَقَبَةً وَ يُطْعِمُ سِتِّينَ مِسْكِيناً قَالَ قُلْتُ يَدْخُلُ فِي هَذَا شَيْ‏ءٌ قَالَ وَ مَا يَدْخُلُ قُلْتُ الْعِيدَانِ وَ أَيَّامُ التَّشْرِيقِ قَالَ يَصُومُهُ فَإِنَّهُ حَقٌّ لَزِمَهُ .

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Upon him is a wergild and a third, and he would Fast two months consecutively from the Sacred months, and he would emancipate (liberate) a neck, and he would feed sixty poor ones’. I said, ‘(Supposing) something enters into this?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And what would it be?’ I said, ‘The two Eids, and the days of Tashreek (11<sup>th</sup>, 12<sup>th</sup>, & 13<sup>th</sup> of Zil-Hijja)?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He would Fast it, for it is a right necessitated upon him’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (16/349)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘Every Fast can be separated except for the three days regarding an expiation for the oath’.

citation.arabic_text: كُلُّ صَوْمٍ يُفَرَّقُ إِلَّا ثَلَاثَةَ أَيَّامٍ فِي كَفَّارَةِ الْيَمِينِ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘Every Fast can be separated except for the three days regarding an expiation for the oath’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (16/349)

text: And from him, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The Fasts of the three days regarding an expiation for the oath are consecutive, there cannot be a gap in between them’.

citation.arabic_text: صِيَامُ ثَلَاثَةِ أَيَّامٍ فِي كَفَّارَةِ الْيَمِينِ مُتَتَابِعَاتٍ لَا يُفْصَلُ بَيْنَهُنَّ .
citation.translation: And from him, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The Fasts of the three days regarding an expiation for the oath are consecutive, there cannot be a gap in between them’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (16/349)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Al Washa, from Aban, from Al Husayn Bin Zayd, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The seven days, and the three days during the Hajj cannot be separated. But rather, these are at the status of the three days regarding the oath’.

citation.arabic_text: السَّبْعَةُ الْأَيَّامِ وَ الثَّلَاثَةُ الْأَيَّامِ فِي الْحَجِّ لَا يُفَرَّقُ إِنَّمَا هِيَ بِمَنْزِلَةِ الثَّلَاثَةِ الْأَيَّامِ فِي الْيَمِينِ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Al Washa, from Aban, from Al Husayn Bin Zayd, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The seven days, and the three days during the Hajj cannot be separated. But rather, these are at the status of the three days regarding the oath’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن أو موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (16/349)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Karram who said, ‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘I made it upon myself that I would be Fasting until the rising of Al-Qaim<sup>asws</sup>’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Fast, and do not Fast during the journey, nor the two Eids, nor the days of Al-Tashreek (11<sup>th</sup>, 12<sup>th</sup> & 13<sup>th</sup> of Zil-Hijja), nor the day wherein is a doubt from a Month of Ramazan’.

citation.arabic_text: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) إِنِّي جَعَلْتُ عَلَى نَفْسِي أَنْ أَصُومَ حَتَّى يَقُومَ الْقَائِمُ ( عليه السلام ) فَقَالَ صُمْ وَ لَا تَصُمْ فِي السَّفَرِ وَ لَا الْعِيدَيْنِ وَ لَا أَيَّامَ التَّشْرِيقِ وَ لَا الْيَوْمَ الَّذِي يُشَكُّ فِيهِ مِنْ شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Karram who said, ‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘I made it upon myself that I would be Fasting until the rising of Al-Qaim<sup>asws</sup>’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Fast, and do not Fast during the journey, nor the two Eids, nor the days of Al-Tashreek (11<sup>th</sup>, 12<sup>th</sup> & 13<sup>th</sup> of Zil-Hijja), nor the day wherein is a doubt from a Month of Ramazan’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن أو موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (6/350)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Ahmad Bin Asheym who said, ‘Al-Husayn wrote to (Imam) Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! A man vows that he would be Fasting for a known (number of) days. So he Fasts some of these, then he fell ill, so he broke. Should he begin his Fasting or can he count with what is past?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> wrote to him: ‘He can count what is past’.

citation.arabic_text: كَتَبَ الْحُسَيْنُ إِلَى الرِّضَا ( عليه السلام ) جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ رَجُلٌ نَذَرَ أَنْ يَصُومَ أَيَّاماً مَعْلُومَةً فَصَامَ بَعْضَهَا ثُمَّ اعْتَلَّ فَأَفْطَرَ أَ يَبْتَدِئُ فِي صَوْمِهِ أَمْ يَحْتَسِبُ بِمَا مَضَى فَكَتَبَ إِلَيْهِ يَحْتَسِبُ مَا مَضَى .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Ahmad Bin Asheym who said, ‘Al-Husayn wrote to (Imam) Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! A man vows that he would be Fasting for a known (number of) days. So he Fasts some of these, then he fell ill, so he broke. citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (6/350)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Salih Bin Abdullah, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! Upon me are Fasts for a month if my uncle would come out from the prison. So he came out. So I woke up in the morning and I intended the Fasting, and one of our companions came over to me. So I called for the lunch and had lunch with him’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem’.

citation.arabic_text: قُلْتُ لَهُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ عَلَيَّ صِيَامُ شَهْرٍ إِنْ خَرَجَ عَمِّي مِنَ الْحَبْسِ فَخَرَجَ فَأُصْبِحُ وَ أَنَا أُرِيدُ الصِّيَامَ فَيَجِيئُنِي بَعْضُ أَصْحَابِنَا فَأَدْعُو بِالْغَدَاءِ وَ أَتَغَدَّى مَعَهُ قَالَ لَا بَأْسَ .

citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (16/350)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Qasim Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ibrahim<sup>asws</sup> (7<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>), said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a man who makes it upon himself the Fasting for a month in Al-Kufa, and a month is Al-Medina, and a month in Al-Makkah, from an affliction he had been afflicted with. So he fulfilled his Fasts for a month in Al-Kufa, and he entered Al-Medina. So he Fasted eighteen days, and the camelier could not remain upon it. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He can Fast what is remaining when he ends up to his city’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ جَعَلَ عَلَى نَفْسِهِ صَوْمَ شَهْرٍ بِالْكُوفَةِ وَ شَهْرٍ بِالْمَدِينَةِ وَ شَهْرٍ بِمَكَّةَ مِنْ بَلَاءٍ ابْتُلِيَ بِهِ فَقُضِيَ أَنَّهُ صَامَ بِالْكُوفَةِ شَهْراً وَ دَخَلَ الْمَدِينَةَ فَصَامَ بِهَا ثَمَانِيَةَ عَشَرَ يَوْماً وَ لَمْ يُقِمْ عَلَيْهِ الْجَمَّالُ قَالَ يَصُومُ مَا بَقِيَ عَلَيْهِ إِذَا انْتَهَى إِلَى بَلَدِهِ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Qasim Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ibrahim<sup>asws</sup> (7<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>), said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a man who makes it upon himself the Fasting for a month in Al-Kufa, and a month is Al-Medina, and a month in Al-Makkah, from an affliction he had been afflicted with. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He can Fast what is remaining when he ends up to his city’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (16/350)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Ja’farasws, from hisasws forefathersasws that Aliasws said regarding a man who vowed that he would be Fasting for a time: ‘The ‘time’ is five months, and the ‘season’ is of six months because Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic is Saying [14:25] Yielding its fruit in every season by the permission of its Lord’.

citation.arabic_text: فِي رَجُلٍ نَذَرَ أَنْ يَصُومَ زَمَاناً قَالَ الزَّمَانُ خَمْسَةُ أَشْهُرٍ وَ الْحِينُ سِتَّةُ أَشْهُرٍ لِأَنَّ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ يَقُولُ تُؤْتِي أُكُلَها كُلَّ حِينٍ بِإِذْنِ رَبِّها .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Ja’farasws, from hisasws forefathersasws that Aliasws said regarding a man who vowed that he would be Fasting for a time: ‘The ‘time’ is five months, and the ‘season’ is of six months because Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic is Saying [14:25] Yielding its fruit in every season by the permission of its Lord’.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Khalid Bin Jareer, from Abu Al Rabi’e, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having been asked about a man who said, ‘By Allahazwj! It is upon me that I Fast for a season’, and that is regarding appreciation. So Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘Someone had come to Aliasws with the likes of this, so heasws said: ‘Fast for six months, for Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic is Saying [14:25] Yielding its fruit in every season by the permission of its Lord – Meaning six months’.

citation.arabic_text: لِلَّهِ عَلَيَّ أَنْ أَصُومَ حِيناً وَ ذَلِكَ فِي شُكْرٍ فَقَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) قَدْ أُتِيَ عَلِيٌّ ( عليه السلام ) فِي مِثْلِ هَذَا فَقَالَ صُمْ سِتَّةَ أَشْهُرٍ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ يَقُولُ تُؤْتِي أُكُلَها كُلَّ حِينٍ بِإِذْنِ رَبِّها يَعْنِي سِتَّةَ أَشْهُرٍ .

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Haroun Bin Muslim, from Mas’ada Bin Sadaqa, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, from his<sup>asws</sup> forefathers<sup>asws</sup> regarding the man who made it upon himself (to Fast) for a specified number of days during every month. Then he travels, so the months pass by him, that he would not be Fasting during the journey, nor would he be making up for it when he is present (back home)’.

citation.arabic_text: الرَّجُلِ يَجْعَلُ عَلَى نَفْسِهِ أَيَّاماً مَعْدُودَةً مُسَمَّاةً فِي كُلِّ شَهْرٍ ثُمَّ يُسَافِرُ فَتَمُرُّ بِهِ الشُّهُورُ أَنَّهُ لَا يَصُومُ فِي السَّفَرِ وَ لَا يَقْضِيهَا إِذَا شَهِدَ .

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bn Mahboub, from Abdullah Bin Sinan who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the man who had timed it upon himself, or he was Fasting from Sacred Months. So the month, and the two month pass by him, not fulfilling it. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He should not be Fasting during the journey, nor would he make up for anything from the optional Fasts except for the three days which he had Fasted from each month, nor make it to be at the status of the Obligatory, except that I<sup>asws</sup> like it for you that you should be habitual upon the righteous deed’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And the one who had the Fasting for the Sacred Months which he used to Fast, it would suffice him in place of each month from the Sacred Months, (the Fasting of) three days’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يَصُومُ صَوْماً قَدْ وَقَّتَهُ عَلَى نَفْسِهِ أَوْ يَصُومُ مِنْ أَشْهُرِ الْحُرُمِ فَيَمُرُّ بِهِ الشَّهْرُ وَ الشَّهْرَانِ لَا يَقْضِيهِ فَقَالَ لَا يَصُومُ فِي السَّفَرِ وَ لَا يَقْضِي شَيْئاً مِنْ صَوْمِ التَّطَوُّعِ إِلَّا الثَّلَاثَةَ الْأَيَّامِ الَّتِي كَانَ يَصُومُهَا مِنْ كُلِّ شَهْرٍ وَ لَا يَجْعَلُهَا بِمَنْزِلَةِ الْوَاجِبِ إِلَّا أَنِّي أُحِبُّ لَكَ أَنْ تَدُومَ عَلَى الْعَمَلِ الصَّالِحِ قَالَ وَ صَاحِبُ الْحُرُمِ الَّذِي كَانَ يَصُومُهَا وَ يُجْزِئُهُ أَنْ يَصُومَ مَكَانَ كُلِّ شَهْرٍ مِنْ أَشْهُرِ الْحُرُمِ ثَلَاثَةَ أَيَّامٍ .

text: Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazal Bin Shazaan, from Ibn Abu Umeyr from Ibrahim Bin Abdul Hameed, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the man who Made it upon himself for the Sake of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic, Fasting of a specified day. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He should be Fasting it for ever, during the journey and the presence (at home)’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يَجْعَلُ لِلَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ عَلَيْهِ صَوْمَ يَوْمٍ مُسَمًّى قَالَ يَصُومُهُ أَبَداً فِي السَّفَرِ وَ الْحَضَرِ .

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Zurara who said, ‘My mother had made it upon herself for the Sake of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, a vow that if Allah<sup>azwj</sup> were to Return one of her children from something which she had feared upon, she would be Fasting that day in which he comes back, for as long as she remained. So she went out with us on a journey to Makkah. So it became doubtful upon us. We did not know whether she should be Fasting or breaking. So I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about that, and I informed him with what she had made it to be upon herself. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘She should not be Fasting during the journey. Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has Exempted it from her His<sup>azwj</sup> Right, and she should be Fasting what she has made it to be upon herself’. He (the narrator) said, ‘What is your<sup>asws</sup> view when she returns and neglects that?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> fear that she might see in that which she had vowed, what she dislikes’.

citation.arabic_text: إِنَّ أُمِّي كَانَتْ جَعَلَتْ عَلَى نَفْسِهَا لِلَّهِ عَلَيْهَا نَذْراً إِنْ كَانَ اللَّهُ رَدَّ عَلَيْهَا بَعْضَ وُلْدِهَا مِنْ شَيْ‏ءٍ كَانَتْ تَخَافُ عَلَيْهِ أَنْ تَصُومَ ذَلِكَ الْيَوْمَ الَّذِي يَقْدَمُ فِيهِ مَا بَقِيَتْ فَخَرَجَتْ مَعَنَا مُسَافِرَةً إِلَى مَكَّةَ فَأَشْكَلَ عَلَيْنَا لَمْ نَدْرِ أَ تَصُومُ أَمْ تُفْطِرُ فَسَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنْ ذَلِكَ وَ أَخْبَرْتُهُ بِمَا جَعَلَتْ عَلَى نَفْسِهَا فَقَالَ لَا تَصُومُ فِي السَّفَرِ قَدْ وَضَعَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا حَقَّهُ وَ تَصُومُ هِيَ مَا جَعَلَتْ عَلَى نَفْسِهَا قَالَ قُلْتُ مَا تَرَى إِذَا هِيَ قَدِمَتْ وَ تَرَكَتْ ذَلِكَ فَقَالَ إِنِّي أَخَافُ أَنْ تَرَى فِي الَّذِي نَذَرَتْ مَا تَكْرَهُ .

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Sahl, from Idrees Bin zayd and Ali Bin Idrees who both said, ‘We asked (Imam) Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> about a man who vowed a vow that if he is freed from the prison, he would be Fasting that day in which he was set free. Then he became frustrated from the Fasting due to an illness which hit him, or other than that. So it prolonged for the man during his lifetime, and a lot of Fasts had gathered upon him. What is the expiation of that Fast?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He can expiate it from each day (by giving charity) with a Mudd (approximately 750g. of food) of wheat, or barley’.

text: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Ays Bin Al Qasim who said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the one who does not Fast the three days from every month, and the Fasting is difficult upon him. Is there a redemption in it?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘A Mudd (approximately 750g. of food) of food regarding each day’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُهُ عَمَّنْ لَمْ يَصُمِ الثَّلَاثَةَ الْأَيَّامِ مِنْ كُلِّ شَهْرٍ وَ هُوَ يَشُدُّ عَلَيْهِ الصِّيَامُ هَلْ فِيهِ فِدَاءٌ قَالَ مُدٌّ مِنْ طَعَامٍ فِي كُلِّ يَوْمٍ .

Is there a redemption in it?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘A Mudd (approximately 750g. of food) of food regarding each day’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (6/356)

text: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Al Washa, from Hammad Bin Usman, from Umar Bin Yazeed who said, ‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘The Fasting is difficult upon me’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘The Dirham you give in charity with is superior than Fasting a day’. Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And I<sup>asws</sup> do not like it if you were to neglect it’.

citation.arabic_text: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) إِنَّ الصَّوْمَ يَشُدُّ عَلَيَّ فَقَالَ لِي لَدِرْهَمٌ تَصَدَّقُ بِهِ أَفْضَلُ مِنْ صِيَامِ يَوْمٍ ثُمَّ قَالَ وَ مَا أُحِبُّ أَنْ تَدَعَهُ .

text: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Yazeed Bin Khaleefa who said, ‘I complained to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, so I said, ‘I tend to get a headache when I Fast these three days, and it is grievous upon me’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So you should do just as I<sup>asws</sup> do when I<sup>asws</sup> travel. So I<sup>asws</sup>, when I<sup>asws</sup> travel, give in charity for each day with a Mudd (approximately 750g. of food) of daily subsistence of my<sup>asws</sup> family which I<sup>asws</sup> tend to provide them with’.

citation.arabic_text: شَكَوْتُ إِلَى أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) فَقُلْتُ إِنِّي أُصَدَّعُ إِذَا صُمْتُ هَذِهِ الثَّلَاثَةَ الْأَيَّامِ وَ يَشُقُّ عَلَيَّ قَالَ فَاصْنَعْ كَمَا أَصْنَعُ إِذَا سَافَرْتُ فَإِنِّي إِذَا سَافَرْتُ تَصَدَّقْتُ عَنْ كُلِّ يَوْمٍ بِمُدٍّ مِنْ قُوتِ أَهْلِي الَّذِي أَقُوتُهُمْ بِهِ .
citation.translation: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Yazeed Bin Khaleefa who said, ‘I complained to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, so I said, ‘I tend to get a headache when I Fast these three days, and it is grievous upon me’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So you should do just as I<sup>asws</sup> do when I<sup>asws</sup> travel. So I<sup>asws</sup>, when I<sup>asws</sup> travel, give in charity for each day with a Mudd (approximately 750g. of food) of daily subsistence of my<sup>asws</sup> family which I<sup>asws</sup> tend to provide them with’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (6/356)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Muhammad Bin Ismail Bin Bazie, from Salih Bin Uqba, from Uqba who said, ‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! I have aged and weakened from Fasting. So how should I deal with these three days during every month?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Uqba! Give in charity with a Dirham for each day’. I said, ‘One Dirham?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Perhaps it is grievous with you, and you are belittling the Dirham’. I said, ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic has Favoured upon me with abundance’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Uqba! Feeding a Muslim is better than Fasting (for) a month’.

citation.arabic_text: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ إِنِّي قَدْ كَبِرْتُ وَ ضَعُفْتُ عَنِ الصِّيَامِ فَكَيْفَ أَصْنَعُ بِهَذِهِ الثَّلَاثَةِ الْأَيَّامِ فِي كُلِّ شَهْرٍ فَقَالَ يَا عُقْبَةُ تَصَدَّقْ بِدِرْهَمٍ عَنْ كُلِّ يَوْمٍ قَالَ قُلْتُ دِرْهَمٌ وَاحِدٌ قَالَ لَعَلَّهَا كَبُرَتْ عِنْدَكَ وَ أَنْتَ تَسْتَقِلُّ الدِّرْهَمَ قَالَ قُلْتُ إِنَّ نِعَمَ اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ عَلَيَّ لَسَابِغَةٌ فَقَالَ يَا عُقْبَةُ لَإِطْعَامُ مُسْلِمٍ خَيْرٌ مِنْ صِيَامِ شَهْرٍ .

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Al Hassan Bin Rashid who said, ‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, or to Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, ‘A man deliberately (postpones) to the month in which the days are shorter, so he Fasts these (optional Fasts) for the year’. He<sup>asws</sup> said; ‘There is no problem’.

citation.arabic_text: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ أَوْ لِأَبِي الْحَسَنِ ( عليه السلام ) الرَّجُلُ يَتَعَمَّدُ الشَّهْرَ فِي الْأَيَّامِ الْقِصَارِ يَصُومُهُ لِسَنَةٍ قَالَ لَا بَأْسَ .

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Ibrahim Bin Mihzam, from Husayn Bin Abu Hamza, from Abu Hamza who said, ‘I said to Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Can I either Fast the three days from each month, or delay it to the winter, then Fast them?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem with that’.

citation.arabic_text: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي جَعْفَرٍ ( عليه السلام ) صَوْمُ ثَلَاثَةِ أَيَّامٍ مِنْ كُلِّ شَهْرٍ أُؤَخِّرُهُ إِلَى الشِّتَاءِ ثُمَّ أَصُومُهَا قَالَ لَا بَأْسَ بِذَلِكَ .

text: Ahmad Bin Idress and Muhammad Bin yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Ahmad Bin Al Hassan, from Amro Bin Saeed, from Musaddaq Bin Sadaqa, from Ammar Bin Musa, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the man who happens to have upon him (the Fasts) from the three days of the month. Is it correct for him that he delays it, or Fasts them during the end of the month?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem’. I said, ‘Can he Fast these successively or separate between them?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Whatever he likes, successively if he so desires to or if he so desires to, he can separate between them’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يَكُونُ عَلَيْهِ مِنَ الثَّلَاثَةِ أَيَّامِ الشَّهْرِ هَلْ يَصْلُحُ لَهُ أَنْ يُؤَخِّرَهَا أَوْ يَصُومُهَا فِي آخِرِ الشَّهْرِ قَالَ لَا بَأْسَ قُلْتُ يَصُومُهَا مُتَوَالِيَةً أَوْ يُفَرِّقُ بَيْنَهَا قَالَ مَا أَحَبَّ إِنْ شَاءَ مُتَوَالِيَةً وَ إِنْ شَاءَ فَرَّقَ بَيْنَهُمَا .

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Safwan Bin Yahya and Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Al A’ala Bin Razeyn, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, (It has been narrated) from one of the two (5<sup>th</sup> or 6<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) having been asked about Fasting the day of Arafat (9<sup>th</sup> Zil-Hijja), so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> do not Fast the day, and it is a day of supplications and the beseeching’.

citation.arabic_text: أَ مَا أَصُومُهُ الْيَوْمَ وَ هُوَ يَوْمُ دُعَاءٍ وَ مَسْأَلَةٍ .

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Sa’alba Bin Maymoun, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said, ‘I heard Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> saying that Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> did not Fast the day of Arafat (9<sup>th</sup> Zil Hijja) since the Fasting of the Month of Ramazan was Revealed’.

citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ إِنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) لَمْ يَصُمْ يَوْمَ عَرَفَةَ مُنْذُ نَزَلَ صِيَامُ شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ .

citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق كالصحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (16/359)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Nuh Bin Shuayb Al Neyshapouri, fom Yaseen Al Zareer, from Hareyz, from Zurara, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> or Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> both having said: ‘Do not Fast during the day of Ashura (10<sup>th</sup> Muharram), nor Arafat (9<sup>th</sup> Zil-Hijja), neither in Makkah, nor in Al-Medina, nor in your hometown, nor in a city from the cities (during these two days)’.

citation.arabic_text: ا لَا تَصُمْ فِي يَوْمِ عَاشُورَاءَ وَ لَا عَرَفَةَ بِمَكَّةَ وَ لَا فِي الْمَدِينَةِ وَ لَا فِي وَطَنِكَ وَ لَا فِي مِصْرٍ مِنَ الْأَمْصَارِ .

text: Al Hassan Bin Ali Al Hashimy, from Muhammad Bin Musa, from Yaqoub Bin Yazeed, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Al Washa who said, ‘My father narrated to me from Najbat Bin Al Haris Al Attar who said, ‘I asked Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> about Fasting the day of Ashura (10<sup>th</sup> Muharram), so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is an abandoned Fast due to the Revelation of the Month of Ramazan, and (practicing) the abandoned is ‘بِدْعَةٌ’ an innovation’. Najba said, ‘So I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> from after his<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> about that, so he<sup>asws</sup> answered me with an answer to that of his<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup>. Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘But, it is a Fast of a day which neither the Book Revealed with it nor did a Sunnah flow with it, except for the sunnah of the progeny of Ziyad due to the killing of Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> Bin Ali<sup>asws</sup>’.

citation.arabic_text: حَدَّثَنِي نَجَبَةُ بْنُ الْحَارِثِ الْعَطَّارُ قَالَ سَأَلْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ ( عليه السلام ) عَنْ صَوْمِ يَوْمِ عَاشُورَاءَ فَقَالَ صَوْمٌ مَتْرُوكٌ بِنُزُولِ شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ وَ الْمَتْرُوكُ بِدْعَةٌ قَالَ نَجَبَةُ فَسَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) مِنْ بَعْدِ أَبِيهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنْ ذَلِكَ فَأَجَابَنِي بِمِثْلِ جَوَابِ أَبِيهِ ثُمَّ قَالَ أَمَا إِنَّهُ صَوْمُ يَوْمٍ مَا نَزَلَ بِهِ كِتَابٌ وَ لَا جَرَتْ بِهِ سُنَّةٌ إِلَّا سُنَّةُ آلِ زِيَادٍ بِقَتْلِ الْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ صَلَوَاتُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِمَا .

text: From him, from Muhammad Bin Isa Bin Ubeyd who said, ‘Ja’far Bin Isa narrated to me from his brother who said, ‘I asked (Imam) Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> about Fasting Ashura (10<sup>th</sup> Muharram) and what the people are saying with regards to it. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is the Fast of Ibn Marjana you are asking me<sup>asws</sup> about. That is a day the pretenders from the Progeny of Ziyad Fasted in, due to the killing of Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup>, and it is a day which the Progeny<sup>asws</sup> of Muhammad<sup>saww</sup> see it as an evil omen (a grievous/tragic day), and the people of Al-Islam see it as an evil omen. And the day which the people of Al-Islam see it as an evil omen can neither be Fasted nor can it be a blissful one. And the day of Wednesday is an inauspicious day. Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Caused His<sup>azwj</sup> Prophet<sup>saww</sup> to pass away during it, and the Progeny<sup>asws</sup> of Muhammad<sup>saww</sup> was not afflicted with except during the day of Wednesday. Thus, we<sup>asws</sup> see it as an evil omen, and our<sup>asws</sup> enemies take it to be blissful/rewarding by it. And, the day of Ashura, Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> was killed, and Ibn Marjana was pleased with it, and the Progeny<sup>asws</sup> of Muhammad<sup>saww</sup> see it as a day of tragedy. Therefore, the one who Fasts it, or sees it to be blessed by it, would meet Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Blessed and High with a morphed heart, and his Resurrection would be with those who made a sunnah of Fasting it and the seekers of the Blessings by it’.

citation.arabic_text: حَدَّثَنِي جَعْفَرُ بْنُ عِيسَى أَخُوهُ قَالَ سَأَلْتُ الرِّضَا ( عليه السلام ) عَنْ صَوْمِ عَاشُورَاءَ وَ مَا يَقُولُ النَّاسُ فِيهِ فَقَالَ عَنْ صَوْمِ ابْنِ مَرْجَانَةَ تَسْأَلُنِي ذَلِكَ يَوْمٌ صَامَهُ الْأَدْعِيَاءُ مِنْ آلِ زِيَادٍ لِقَتْلِ الْحُسَيْنِ ( عليه السلام ) وَ هُوَ يَوْمٌ يَتَشَأَّمُ بِهِ آلُ مُحَمَّدٍ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) وَ يَتَشَأَّمُ بِهِ أَهْلُ الْإِسْلَامِ وَ الْيَوْمُ الَّذِي يَتَشَأَّمُ بِهِ أَهْلُ الْإِسْلَامِ لَا يُصَامُ وَ لَا يُتَبَرَّكُ بِهِ وَ يَوْمُ الْإِثْنَيْنِ يَوْمُ نَحْسٌ قَبَضَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ فِيهِ نَبِيَّهُ وَ مَا أُصِيبَ آلُ مُحَمَّدٍ إِلَّا فِي يَوْمِ الْإِثْنَيْنِ فَتَشَأَّمْنَا بِهِ وَ تَبَرَّكَ بِهِ عَدُوُّنَا وَ يَوْمُ عَاشُورَاءَ قُتِلَ الْحُسَيْنُ صَلَوَاتُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ وَ تَبَرَّكَ بِهِ ابْنُ مَرْجَانَةَ وَ تَشَأَّمَ بِهِ آلُ مُحَمَّدٍ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ فَمَنْ صَامَهُمَا أَوْ تَبَرَّكَ بِهِمَا لَقِيَ اللَّهَ تَبَارَكَ وَ تَعَالَى مَمْسُوخَ الْقَلْبِ وَ كَانَ حَشْرُهُ مَعَ الَّذِينَ سَنُّوا صَوْمَهُمَا وَ التَّبَرُّكَ بِهِمَا .

text: And from him, from Muhammad Bin Isa who said, ‘Muhammad in Abu Umeyr narrated to us, from Zayd Al Narsy who said, ‘I heard Zurara asking Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the Fasting of the day of Ashura (10<sup>th</sup> Muharram). So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The one who Fasts it, his share from the Fast of that day would be a share of Ibn Marjana and the progeny of Ziyad’. I said, ‘And what is their share from that day?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The Fire. We<sup>asws</sup> seek Refuge with Allah<sup>azwj</sup> from the Fire and from the deed which takes one closer to the Fire’.

citation.arabic_text: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ زَيْدٍ النَّرْسِيِّ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ عُبَيْدَ بْنَ زُرَارَةَ يَسْأَلُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنْ صَوْمِ يَوْمِ عَاشُورَاءَ فَقَالَ مَنْ صَامَهُ كَانَ حَظُّهُ مِنْ صِيَامِ ذَلِكَ الْيَوْمِ حَظَّ ابْنِ مَرْجَانَةَ وَ آلِ زِيَادٍ قَالَ قُلْتُ وَ مَا كَانَ حَظُّهُمْ مِنْ ذَلِكَ الْيَوْمِ قَالَ النَّارُ أَعَاذَنَا اللَّهُ مِنَ النَّارِ وَ مِنْ عَمَلٍ يُقَرِّبُ مِنَ النَّارِ .
citation.translation: And from him, from Muhammad Bin Isa who said, ‘Muhammad in Abu Umeyr narrated to us, from Zayd Al Narsy who said, ‘I heard Zurara asking Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the Fasting of the day of Ashura (10<sup>th</sup> Muharram). So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The one who Fasts it, his share from the Fast of that day would be a share of Ibn Marjana and the progeny of Ziyad’. I said, ‘And what is their share from that day?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The Fire. We<sup>asws</sup> seek Refuge with Allah<sup>azwj</sup> from the Fire and from the deed which takes one closer to the Fire’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (6/362)

text: And from him, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Aban, from Abdul Malik who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the Fast of ‘Tasua’ (9<sup>th</sup> Muharram), and Ashura (10<sup>th</sup> Muharram) from the month of Muharram. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Tasua is a day in which Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> and his<sup>asws</sup> companions, may Allah<sup>azwj</sup> be Pleased with them, were surrounded in Kerbala, and the cavalries of the people of Syria were gathered against him<sup>asws</sup>, and inflicted injuries upon him<sup>asws</sup>; and Ibn Marjana and Umar Bin Sa’ad were joyful due to the large numbers of the cavalries and its abundance, and Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> and his<sup>asws</sup> companions, may Allah<sup>azwj</sup> be Pleased with them, were weakened during it, and they were convinced that no helper would be coming to Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> nor would the people of Al-Iraq support him<sup>asws</sup>. By my<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup>, the oppressed, the alienated. Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And as for the day of Ashura, so it is a day in which Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> was injured to bits between his<sup>asws</sup> companions, and his<sup>asws</sup> companions were injured to bits around him<sup>asws</sup>, stripped. So, can a Fast happen to be during that day? Never! By the Lord<sup>azwj</sup> of the Sacred House, it is not a day of Fasting, and it is not except for a day of grief, and the difficulties enter upon the inhabitants of the sky and the inhabitants of the earth, and the entirety of the Believers. And, it is a day of happiness and joy for Ibn Marjana and the progeny of Ziyad, and the people of Syria. May Allah<sup>azwj</sup> be Wrathful upon them and upon their offspring. And, that is a day in which the entirety of the spots of the earth wailed upon him<sup>asws</sup> except for the spot of Syria. So the one who Fasts, or (believes to be) fortunate by it, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Resurrect him with the progeny of Ziyad, morphed of the heart, Angered upon; and the one who hoards provisions in his house, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> the Exalted would Cause his end result for hypocrisy to be in his heart up to the day he meets Him<sup>azwj</sup>, and Snatch away the Blessings from him, and from the people of his household, and his children, and the Satan<sup>la</sup> would be his participant in the entirety of that’.

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at who said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the Fasts of the day of Al-Fitr (Eid), so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is not befitting to Fast it, nor Fasting the days of Al-Tashreek (11<sup>th</sup>, 12<sup>th</sup> & 13<sup>th</sup> Zil Hijja)’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ صِيَامِ يَوْمِ الْفِطْرِ فَقَالَ لَا يَنْبَغِي صِيَامُهُ وَ لَا صِيَامُ أَيَّامِ التَّشْرِيقِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at who said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the Fasts of the day of Al-Fitr (Eid), so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is not befitting to Fast it, nor Fasting the days of Al-Tashreek (11<sup>th</sup>, 12<sup>th</sup> & 13<sup>th</sup> Zil Hijja)’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (16/363)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Abu Saeed Al Mukary, from Ziyad Bin Abu Al Hallal who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said to us: ‘Do not Fast after the (Eid) Al-Azha for three days, nor after (Eid) Al-Fitr for three days. These are the days of eating and drinking’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ لَنَا أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) لَا صِيَامَ بَعْدَ الْأَضْحَى ثَلَاثَةَ أَيَّامٍ وَ لَا بَعْدَ الْفِطْرِ ثَلَاثَةَ أَيَّامٍ إِنَّهَا أَيَّامُ أَكْلٍ وَ شُرْبٍ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Abu Saeed Al Mukary, from Ziyad Bin Abu Al Hallal who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said to us: ‘Do not Fast after the (Eid) Al-Azha for three days, nor after (Eid) Al-Fitr for three days. These are the days of eating and drinking’.

text: Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, from Safwan Bin Yahya, and Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abdul Rahman Bin Al Hajjaj who said, ‘I asked Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> about the two days which are after the (Eid) Al-Fitr, can one Fast them or not?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> dislike for you that you Fast these two’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا الْحَسَنِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنِ الْيَوْمَيْنِ اللَّذَيْنِ بَعْدَ الْفِطْرِ أَ يُصَامَانِ أَمْ لَا فَقَالَ أَكْرَهُ لَكَ أَنْ تَصُومَهُمَا .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, from Safwan Bin Yahya, and Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abdul Rahman Bin Al Hajjaj who said, ‘I asked Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> about the two days which are after the (Eid) Al-Fitr, can one Fast them or not?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> dislike for you that you Fast these two’.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Qasim Bin Yahya, from grandfather Al Hassan Bin Rashid, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! Is there for the Muslims an Eid other than the two Eids?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, O Hassan, one greater than these two and more noble’. I said, ‘And which day is it?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is the day in which Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> was nominated as a flag for the people’. I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! And what is befitting for us that we should be doing during it?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘You should be Fasting it, O Hassan, and frequenting the Salawaat upon Muhammad<sup>asws</sup> and the Progeny<sup>asws</sup> of Muhammad<sup>saww</sup>, and disavowing to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> from the one who oppressed them, for the Prophets<sup>as</sup> used to order the<sup>as</sup> successors<sup>as</sup> with the day in which the successor<sup>as</sup> was nominated in, that they (the people) should be taking it as an Eid’. He (the narrator) said, ‘I said, ‘So what is for the one who Fasts it?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The Fasts of sixty months; and do not leave the Fast of the twenty seventh of Rajab, for it is the day in which the Prophet-hood descended upon Muhammad<sup>saww</sup>, and its Reward is like sixty months for you’.

citation.arabic_text: قُلْتُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ لِلْمُسْلِمِينَ عِيدٌ غَيْرَ الْعِيدَيْنِ قَالَ نَعَمْ يَا حَسَنُ أَعْظَمُهُمَا وَ أَشْرَفُهُمَا قُلْتُ وَ أَيُّ يَوْمٍ هُوَ قَالَ هُوَ يَوْمٌ نُصِبَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ صَلَوَاتُ اللَّهِ وَ سَلَامُهُ عَلَيْهِ فِيهِ عَلَماً لِلنَّاسِ قُلْتُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ وَ مَا يَنْبَغِي لَنَا أَنْ نَصْنَعَ فِيهِ قَالَ تَصُومُهُ يَا حَسَنُ وَ تُكْثِرُ الصَّلَاةَ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَ آلِهِ وَ تَبَرَّأُ إِلَى اللَّهِ مِمَّنْ ظَلَمَهُمْ فَإِنَّ الْأَنْبِيَاءَ صَلَوَاتُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِمْ كَانَتْ تَأْمُرُ الْأَوْصِيَاءَ بِالْيَوْمِ الَّذِي كَانَ يُقَامُ فِيهِ الْوَصِيُّ أَنْ يُتَّخَذَ عِيداً قَالَ قُلْتُ فَمَا لِمَنْ صَامَهُ قَالَ صِيَامُ سِتِّينَ شَهْراً وَ لَا تَدَعْ صِيَامَ يَوْمِ سَبْعٍ وَ عِشْرِينَ مِنْ رَجَبٍ فَإِنَّهُ هُوَ الْيَوْمُ الَّذِي نَزَلَتْ فِيهِ النُّبُوَّةُ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) وَ ثَوَابُهُ مِثْلُ سِتِّينَ شَهْراً لَكُمْ .

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from one of our companions, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> the 1<sup>st</sup> having said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Appointed Muhammad<sup>saww</sup> as a Mercy to the worlds during the 27<sup>th</sup> of Rajab. So the one who Fasts that day, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Write for him the Fasts of sixty months. And, during the twenty fifth of Zil-Qadah, the House (Kabah) was Placed, and it is the first Mercy Placed upon the face of the earth. Therefore, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Made it as a resort and a security for the people. So the one who Fasts that day, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Write for him the Fasts of sixty months; And during the first day of Zil-Hijjaj, Ibrahim<sup>as</sup> the Friend of the beneficent was born, so the one who Fasts that day, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Write for him the Fasts of sixty months’.

citation.arabic_text: بَعَثَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ مُحَمَّداً ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) رَحْمَةً لِلْعَالَمِينَ فِي سَبْعٍ وَ عِشْرِينَ مِنْ رَجَبٍ فَمَنْ صَامَ ذَلِكَ الْيَوْمَ كَتَبَ اللَّهُ لَهُ صِيَامَ سِتِّينَ شَهْراً وَ فِي خَمْسَةٍ وَ عِشْرِينَ مِنْ ذِي الْقَعْدَةِ وُضِعَ الْبَيْتُ وَ هُوَ أَوَّلُ رَحْمَةٍ وُضِعَتْ عَلَى وَجْهِ الْأَرْضِ فَجَعَلَهُ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ مَثَابَةً لِلنَّاسِ وَ أَمْناً فَمَنْ صَامَ ذَلِكَ الْيَوْمَ كَتَبَ اللَّهُ لَهُ صِيَامَ سِتِّينَ شَهْراً وَ فِي أَوَّلِ يَوْمٍ مِنْ ذِي الْحِجَّةِ وُلِدَ إِبْرَاهِيمُ خَلِيلُ الرَّحْمَنِ ( عليه السلام ) فَمَنْ صَامَ ذَلِكَ الْيَوْمَ كَتَبَ اللَّهُ لَهُ صِيَامَ سِتِّينَ شَهْراً.
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from one of our companions, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> the 1<sup>st</sup> having said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Appointed Muhammad<sup>saww</sup> as a Mercy to the worlds during the 27<sup>th</sup> of Rajab. So the one who Fasts that day, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Write for him the Fasts of sixty months. And, during the twenty fifth of Zil-Qadah, the House (Kabah) was Placed, and it is the first Mercy Placed upon the face of the earth. Therefore, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Made it as a resort and a security for the people. So the one who Fasts that day, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Write for him the Fasts of sixty months; And during the first day of Zil-Hijjaj, Ibrahim<sup>as</sup> the Friend of the beneficent was born, so the one who Fasts that day, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Write for him the Fasts of sixty months’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (6/365)

text: Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Abdul Rahman Bin Salim, from his father who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Is there an Eid for the Muslims apart from the day of Friday, and Al-Azha, and Al-Fitr?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, one greater than that in sanctity’. I said, ‘And which Eid is it, may I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The day during which Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> nominated Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> and said: ‘The one whose Master I<sup>saww</sup> was, so Ali<sup>asws</sup> is his Master’. I said, ‘And which day was it?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘What would you do with the (particular) day as the year circulates. But, it was the 18<sup>th</sup> of Zilhajj’. So I said, ‘And is befitting for us that we should be doing during that day?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Mentioning Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, Mighty is His<sup>azwj</sup> Mention, during it with the Fasting, and the worship, and the mention of Muhammad<sup>saww</sup> and the Progeny<sup>asws</sup> of Muhammad<sup>saww</sup>, for Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> bequeathed Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> that he<sup>asws</sup> should be taking it as an Eid, and similar to that is what the Prophets<sup>as</sup> used to bequeath their<sup>as</sup> successors<sup>as</sup> with that, therefore take it as an Eid’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) هَلْ لِلْمُسْلِمِينَ عِيدٌ غَيْرَ يَوْمِ الْجُمُعَةِ وَ الْأَضْحَى وَ الْفِطْرِ قَالَ نَعَمْ أَعْظَمُهَا حُرْمَةً قُلْتُ وَ أَيُّ عِيدٍ هُوَ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ قَالَ الْيَوْمُ الَّذِي نَصَبَ فِيهِ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) وَ قَالَ مَنْ كُنْتُ مَوْلَاهُ فَعَلِيٌّ مَوْلَاهُ قُلْتُ وَ أَيُّ يَوْمٍ هُوَ قَالَ وَ مَا تَصْنَعُ بِالْيَوْمِ إِنَّ السَّنَةَ تَدُورُ وَ لَكِنَّهُ يَوْمُ ثَمَانِيَةَ عَشَرَ مِنْ ذِي الْحِجَّةِ فَقُلْتُ وَ مَا يَنْبَغِي لَنَا أَنْ نَفْعَلَ فِي ذَلِكَ الْيَوْمِ قَالَ تَذْكُرُونَ اللَّهَ عَزَّ ذِكْرُهُ فِيهِ بِالصِّيَامِ وَ الْعِبَادَةِ وَ الذِّكْرِ لِمُحَمَّدٍ وَ آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ فَإِنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) أَوْصَى أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) أَنْ يَتَّخِذَ ذَلِكَ الْيَوْمَ عِيداً وَ كَذَلِكَ كَانَتِ الْأَنْبِيَاءُ ( عليهم السلام ) تَفْعَلُ كَانُوا يُوصُونَ أَوْصِيَاءَهُمْ بِذَلِكَ فَيَتَّخِذُونَهُ عِيداً .

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Yusuf Bin Al Sukht, from Hamdan Bin Al Nazar, from Muhammad Bin Abdullah Al Sayqal who said, ‘Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, meaning Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> came out to us during the twenty fifth day of Zil-Qadah, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Fast, for I<sup>asws</sup> am Fasting’. We said, ‘May we be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! Which day is it?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is a day in which the Mercy was Deployed, and the land was Spread during it, and the Kabah was established during it, and Adam<sup>as</sup> descended during it’.

citation.arabic_text: خَرَجَ عَلَيْنَا أَبُو الْحَسَنِ يَعْنِي الرِّضَا ( عليه السلام ) فِي يَوْمِ خَمْسَةٍ وَ عِشْرِينَ مِنْ ذِي الْقَعْدَةِ فَقَالَ صُومُوا فَإِنِّي أَصْبَحْتُ صَائِماً قُلْنَا جُعِلْنَا فِدَاكَ أَيُّ يَوْمٍ هُوَ فَقَالَ يَوْمٌ نُشِرَتْ فِيهِ الرَّحْمَةُ وَ دُحِيَتْ فِيهِ الْأَرْضُ وَ نُصِبَتْ فِيهِ الْكَعْبَةُ وَ هَبَطَ فِيهِ آدَمُ ( عليه السلام ) .

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Your breaking the Fast for your Believing brother is superior to your own optional Fast’.

citation.arabic_text: إِفْطَارُكَ لِأَخِيكَ الْمُؤْمِنِ أَفْضَلُ مِنْ صِيَامِكَ تَطَوُّعاً .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Your breaking the Fast for your Believing brother is superior to your own optional Fast’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (16/368)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Barqy, from Al Qasim Bin Muhammad, from Al Ays, from Najam Bin Huteym, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’farasws having said: ‘The one who intends the Fasting, then goes over to his brother, so he asks him that he should break in his presence, so let him break, and let him enter the joy upon him, for it (the Fast) of that day would be Counted for him as ten days; and these are the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [6:160] Whoever comes with a good deed, he shall have ten like it’.

citation.arabic_text: مَنْ نَوَى الصَّوْمَ ثُمَّ دَخَلَ عَلَى أَخِيهِ فَسَأَلَهُ أَنْ يُفْطِرَ عِنْدَهُ فَلْيُفْطِرْ وَ لْيُدْخِلْ عَلَيْهِ السُّرُورَ فَإِنَّهُ يُحْتَسَبُ لَهُ بِذَلِكَ الْيَوْمِ عَشَرَةُ أَيَّامٍ وَ هُوَ قَوْلُ اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ مَنْ جاءَ بِالْحَسَنَةِ فَلَهُ عَشْرُ أَمْثالِها .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Barqy, from Al Qasim Bin Muhammad, from Al Ays, from Najam Bin Huteym, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’farasws having said: ‘The one who intends the Fasting, then goes over to his brother, so he asks him that he should break in his presence, so let him break, and let him enter the joy upon him, for it (the Fast) of that day would be Counted for him as ten days; and these are the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [6:160] Whoever comes with a good deed, he shall have ten like it’.

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Salih Bin Uqba, from Jameel Bin Darraj who said, ‘Abu Abullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The one who goes over to his brother and he is Fasting, so he breaks in his presence and he does not let him know of his Fast that he is doing him a favour, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Write for him the Fasts of a year’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) مَنْ دَخَلَ عَلَى أَخِيهِ وَ هُوَ صَائِمٌ فَأَفْطَرَ عِنْدَهُ وَ لَمْ يُعْلِمْهُ بِصَوْمِهِ فَيَمُنَّ عَلَيْهِ كَتَبَ اللَّهُ لَهُ صَوْمَ سَنَةٍ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Salih Bin Uqba, from Jameel Bin Darraj who said, ‘Abu Abullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The one who goes over to his brother and he is Fasting, so he breaks in his presence and he does not let him know of his Fast that he is doing him a favour, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Write for him the Fasts of a year’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (16/369)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Al Deynawry, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Salih Bin Uqba who said, ‘I went over to Jameel Bin Darraj and in front of him was a meal, eating eagerly from it. So he said, ‘Approach and eat’. So I said, ‘I am Fasting’. So he neglected me until when he had eaten it, and there did not remain from it except for a little, he insisted upon me, ‘Will you not break?’ So I said to him, ‘Why did you not insist before this time?’ So he said, ‘I wanted to educate you with that’. Then he said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Whichever Believing man goes over to his brother and he is Fasting, so he asks him to eat, and he does not inform him of his Fasting to favour upon him with his breaking, Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, Majestic is His<sup>azwj</sup> Praise, would Write for that day for him, the Fasts of a year’.

citation.arabic_text: دَخَلْتُ عَلَى جَمِيلِ بْنِ دَرَّاجٍ وَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ خِوَانٌ عَلَيْهِ غَسَّانِيَّةٌ يَأْكُلُ مِنْهَا فَقَالَ ادْنُ فَكُلْ فَقُلْتُ إِنِّي صَائِمٌ فَتَرَكَنِي حَتَّى إِذَا أَكَلَهَا فَلَمْ يَبْقَ مِنْهَا إِلَّا الْيَسِيرُ عَزَمَ عَلَيَّ أَلَّا أَفْطَرْتَ فَقُلْتُ لَهُ أَلَّا كَانَ هَذَا قَبْلَ السَّاعَةِ فَقَالَ أَرَدْتُ بِذَلِكَ أَدَبَكَ ثُمَّ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ أَيُّمَا رَجُلٍ مُؤْمِنٍ دَخَلَ عَلَى أَخِيهِ وَ هُوَ صَائِمٌ فَسَأَلَهُ الْأَكْلَ فَلَمْ يُخْبِرْهُ بِصِيَامِهِ لِيَمُنَّ عَلَيْهِ بِإِفْطَارِهِ كَتَبَ اللَّهُ جَلَّ ثَنَاؤُهُ لَهُ بِذَلِكَ الْيَوْمِ صِيَامَ سَنَةٍ .

text: Ali Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Jamhour, from one of his companions, from Ali Bin Hadeed who said, ‘I said to Abu Al-Hassan Al-Maazy<sup>asws</sup> (7<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>), ‘I go over to the group of people and they are eating, and Al-Asr has arrived, and I am Fasting. So they are saying, ‘Break’’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Break, for it is superior’.

citation.arabic_text: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي الْحَسَنِ الْمَاضِي ( عليه السلام ) أَدْخُلُ عَلَى الْقَوْمِ وَ هُمْ يَأْكُلُونَ وَ قَدْ صَلَّيْتُ الْعَصْرَ وَ أَنَا صَائِمٌ فَيَقُولُونَ أَفْطِرْ فَقَالَ أَفْطِرْ فَإِنَّهُ أَفْضَلُ .

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Hassan Bin Ibrahim Bin sufyan, from Dawood Al Raqqy who said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘You breaking of your Fast in a house of your Muslim brother is superior than your Fasting seventy times over, or ninety times’.

citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ لَإِفْطَارُكَ فِي مَنْزِلِ أَخِيكَ الْمُسْلِمِ أَفْضَلُ مِنْ صِيَامِكَ سَبْعِينَ ضِعْفاً أَوْ تِسْعِينَ ضِعْفاً .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Hassan Bin Ibrahim Bin sufyan, from Dawood Al Raqqy who said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘You breaking of your Fast in a house of your Muslim brother is superior than your Fasting seventy times over, or ninety times’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (16/370)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Al Qasim Bin Urwa, from one of his companions, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘It is not correct for the wife that she Fasts the optional Fast except by the permission of her husband’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ لَا يَصْلُحُ لِلْمَرْأَةِ أَنْ تَصُومَ تَطَوُّعاً إِلَّا بِإِذْنِ زَوْجِهَا .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Al Qasim Bin Urwa, from one of his companions, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘It is not correct for the wife that she Fasts the optional Fast except by the permission of her husband’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرسل - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (6/371)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Ahmad Bin Hilal, from Marwak Bin Ubeyd, from Nasheet Bin Salih, from Hisham Bin Al Hakam, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘It is from an understanding of the guest that he would not Fast voluntarily except by the permission of his host; and from the obedience of the wife to her husband is that she would not be Fasting voluntarily (optional Fasts) except by his permission; and from the correctness of the slave and his obedience, and his correctness to his master that he would not be Fasting voluntarily except by the permission of his master and his instruction; and from the righteousness of the child that he would not Fast voluntarily except by the permission of his parents, and their instruction – or else the guest would be ignorant, and the wife would be disobedient, and the slave would be wicked, disobedient, and the child would be disloyal’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) مِنْ فِقْهِ الضَّيْفِ أَنْ لَا يَصُومَ تَطَوُّعاً إِلَّا بِإِذْنِ صَاحِبِهِ وَ مِنْ طَاعَةِ الْمَرْأَةِ لِزَوْجِهَا أَنْ لَا تَصُومَ تَطَوُّعاً إِلَّا بِإِذْنِهِ وَ أَمْرِهِ وَ مِنْ صَلَاحِ الْعَبْدِ وَ طَاعَتِهِ وَ نُصْحِهِ لِمَوْلَاهُ أَنْ لَا يَصُومَ تَطَوُّعاً إِلَّا بِإِذْنِ مَوْلَاهُ وَ أَمْرِهِ وَ مِنْ بِرِّ الْوَلَدِ أَنْ لَا يَصُومَ تَطَوُّعاً إِلَّا بِإِذْنِ أَبَوَيْهِ وَ أَمْرِهِمَا وَ إِلَّا كَانَ الضَّيْفُ جَاهِلًا وَ كَانَتِ الْمَرْأَةُ عَاصِيَةً وَ كَانَ الْعَبْدُ فَاسِقاً عَاصِياً وَ كَانَ الْوَلَدُ عَاقّاً .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Ahmad Bin Hilal, from Marwak Bin Ubeyd, from Nasheet Bin Salih, from Hisham Bin Al Hakam, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘It is from an understanding of the guest that he would not Fast voluntarily except by the permission of his host; and from the obedience of the wife to her husband is that she would not be Fasting voluntarily (optional Fasts) except by his permission; and from the correctness of the slave and his obedience, and his correctness to his master that he would not be Fasting voluntarily except by the permission of his master and his instruction; and from the righteousness of the child that he would not Fast voluntarily except by the permission of his parents, and their instruction – or else the guest would be ignorant, and the wife would be disobedient, and the slave would be wicked, disobedient, and the child would be disloyal’.

text: Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Bundar and someone else, from Ibrahim Bin Is’haq, by a chain he mentioned, from Al Fuzayl Bin Yasaar, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘When a man enters a city, so he is a guest upon the ones who are in it, from the people of his Religion, until he departs from them. And, it is not befitting for the guest that he should be Fasting except with their permission, perhaps they would be making something, so it would spoil upon them. And, it is not befitting for them that they should be Fasting except with the permission of the guest, perhaps he would be embarrassed, so he would desire the food, but he would leave it for them’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) إِذَا دَخَلَ رَجُلٌ بَلْدَةً فَهُوَ ضَيْفٌ عَلَى مَنْ بِهَا مِنْ أَهْلِ دِينِهِ حَتَّى يَرْحَلَ عَنْهُمْ وَ لَا يَنْبَغِي لِلضَّيْفِ أَنْ يَصُومَ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِهِمْ لِئَلَّا يَعْمَلُوا الشَّيْ‏ءَ فَيَفْسُدَ عَلَيْهِمْ وَ لَا يَنْبَغِي لَهُمْ أَنْ يَصُومُوا إِلَّا بِإِذْنِ الضَّيْفِ لِئَلَّا يَحْتَشِمَهُمْ فَيَشْتَهِيَ الطَّعَامَ فَيَتْرُكَهُ لَهُمْ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Bundar and someone else, from Ibrahim Bin Is’haq, by a chain he mentioned, from Al Fuzayl Bin Yasaar, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘When a man enters a city, so he is a guest upon the ones who are in it, from the people of his Religion, until he departs from them. And, it is not befitting for them that they should be Fasting except with the permission of the guest, perhaps he would be embarrassed, so he would desire the food, but he would leave it for them’.

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Malik Bin Atiyya, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The Prophet<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘It is not for the wife that she should be Fasting voluntarily (optional Fast) except by the permission of her husband’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) لَيْسَ لِلْمَرْأَةِ أَنْ تَصُومَ تَطَوُّعاً إِلَّا بِإِذْنِ زَوْجِهَا .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Malik Bin Atiyya, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The Prophet<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘It is not for the wife that she should be Fasting voluntarily (optional Fast) except by the permission of her husband’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (6/372)

text: Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Bundar, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Al Jamourany, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Amro Bin Jubeyr Al Azramy, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘A woman came over to the Prophet<sup>saww</sup>, so she said, ‘O Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>! What is a right of the husband upon the wife?’ So he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘There is a lot from that’. So she said, ‘Inform me with something from that’. So he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘It is not for her that she should be Fasting except by his permission’.

citation.arabic_text: جَاءَتِ امْرَأَةٌ إِلَى النَّبِيِّ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) فَقَالَتْ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ مَا حَقُّ الزَّوْجِ عَلَى الْمَرْأَةِ فَقَالَ هُوَ أَكْثَرُ مِنْ ذَلِكَ فَقَالَتْ أَخْبِرْنِي بِشَيْ‏ءٍ مِنْ ذَلِكَ فَقَالَ لَيْسَ لَهَا أَنْ تَصُومَ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِهِ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Bundar, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Al Jamourany, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Amro Bin Jubeyr Al Azramy, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘A woman came over to the Prophet<sup>saww</sup>, so she said, ‘O Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>! What is a right of the husband upon the wife?’ So he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘There is a lot from that’. So she said, ‘Inform me with something from that’. So he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘It is not for her that she should be Fasting except by his permission’.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, from his<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, when he<sup>saww</sup> was Fasting, so if he<sup>saww</sup> could not find the sweet, would break Fast upon the water’.

citation.arabic_text: كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) إِذَا صَامَ فَلَمْ يَجِدِ الْحَلْوَاءَ أَفْطَرَ عَلَى الْمَاءِ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, from his<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, when he<sup>saww</sup> was Fasting, so if he<sup>saww</sup> could not find the sweet, would break Fast upon the water’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (16/373)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim,from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from a man, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘When the man breaks a Fast upon the lukewarm water, it cleans his liver and washes the sins from ‘الْقَلْبِ’ the heart, and strengthens the vision and the glare’.

citation.arabic_text: إِذَا أَفْطَرَ الرَّجُلُ عَلَى الْمَاءِ الْفَاتِرِ نَقَّى كَبِدَهُ وَ غَسَلَ الذُّنُوبَ مِنَ الْقَلْبِ وَ قَوَّى الْبَصَرَ وَ الْحَدَقَ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim,from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from a man, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘When the man breaks a Fast upon the lukewarm water, it cleans his liver and washes the sins from ‘الْقَلْبِ’ the heart, and strengthens the vision and the glare’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (6/373)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Salih Bin Sindy, from Ibn Sinan, from a man, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Breaking a Fast upon the water washes the sins from the ‘Qalb’ (heart)’.

citation.arabic_text: الْإِفْطَارُ عَلَى الْمَاءِ يَغْسِلُ الذُّنُوبَ مِنَ الْقَلْبِ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Salih Bin Sindy, from Ibn Sinan, from a man, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Breaking a Fast upon the water washes the sins from the ‘Qalb’ (heart)’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (16/373)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from the one who mentioned it, from Mansour Bin Al Abbas, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Muskan, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, whenever he<sup>saww</sup> broke a Fast, began with a sweet, breaking upon it. So if he<sup>saww</sup> could not find, so a (lump of) sugar, or dates. So if all of that was not available, so lukewarm water; and he<sup>saww</sup> was saying: ‘It cleans the stomach and the liver, and aromatises the breath and the mouth, and it strengthens the teeth, and strengthens the glare, and polishes the vision, and washes the sins with a washing, and settles the veins and the gallbladder, and the overcoming bitterness, and cuts the phlegm, and extinguishes the heat from the stomach, and removes the headaches’.

citation.arabic_text: كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) إِذَا أَفْطَرَ بَدَأَ بِحَلْوَاءَ يُفْطِرُ عَلَيْهَا فَإِنْ لَمْ يَجِدْ فَسُكَّرَةٍ أَوْ تَمَرَاتٍ فَإِذَا أَعْوَزَ ذَلِكَ كُلُّهُ فَمَاءٍ فَاتِرٍ وَ كَانَ يَقُولُ يُنَقِّي الْمَعِدَةَ وَ الْكَبِدَ وَ يُطَيِّبُ النَّكْهَةَ وَ الْفَمَ وَ يُقَوِّي الْأَضْرَاسَ وَ يُقَوِّي الْحَدَقَ وَ يَجْلُو النَّاظِرَ وَ يَغْسِلُ الذُّنُوبَ غَسْلًا وَ يُسَكِّنُ الْعُرُوقَ الْهَائِجَةَ وَ الْمِرَّةَ الْغَالِبَةَ وَ يَقْطَعُ الْبَلْغَمَ وَ يُطْفِئُ الْحَرَارَةَ عَنِ الْمَعِدَةِ وَ يَذْهَبُ بِالصُّدَاعِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from the one who mentioned it, from Mansour Bin Al Abbas, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Muskan, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, whenever he<sup>saww</sup> broke a Fast, began with a sweet, breaking upon it. So if he<sup>saww</sup> could not find, so a (lump of) sugar, or dates. So if all of that was not available, so lukewarm water; and he<sup>saww</sup> was saying: ‘It cleans the stomach and the liver, and aromatises the breath and the mouth, and it strengthens the teeth, and strengthens the glare, and polishes the vision, and washes the sins with a washing, and settles the veins and the gallbladder, and the overcoming bitterness, and cuts the phlegm, and extinguishes the heat from the stomach, and removes the headaches’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (16/374)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ibrahim Bin Mihzan, from Talha Bin Zayd, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> used to break a Fast upon the dates during the season of the dates, and upon fresh dates during the season of fresh dates’.

citation.arabic_text: كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) يُفْطِرُ عَلَى التَّمْرِ فِي زَمَنِ التَّمْرِ وَ عَلَى الرُّطَبِ فِي زَمَنِ الرُّطَبِ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ibrahim Bin Mihzan, from Talha Bin Zayd, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> used to break a Fast upon the dates during the season of the dates, and upon fresh dates during the season of fresh dates’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور لكنه قوي - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (6/374)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ja’far Bin Abdullah Al Ashary, from Ibn Al Qaddah, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, the first of what he<sup>saww</sup> used to break a Fast upon during a season of the fresh dates, was fresh dates, and during a season of dates, the dates’.

citation.arabic_text: كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) أَوَّلُ مَا يُفْطِرُ عَلَيْهِ فِي زَمَنِ الرُّطَبِ الرُّطَبُ وَ فِي زَمَنِ التَّمْرِ التَّمْرُ .
